Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Tardigrades, microscopic animals often called water bears, can survive conditions that would kill almost any other organism. When their environment dries out, they curl into a dormant state called a tun, reducing their metabolism to less than 0.01 percent of normal. In this state, tardigrades have endured freezing temperatures, intense radiation, and even exposure to the vacuum of space. Researchers studying a protein unique to tardigrades, called Dsup, found that it shields their DNA from radiation damage, offering one explanation for the animals' remarkable resilience.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that tardigrades should be sent on future space missions
To compare tardigrades with other microscopic animals
To describe tardigrades' ability to survive extreme conditions and one possible reason for it
To explain how scientists first discovered tardigrades
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn tardigradlarning ekstremal sharoitlarda yashay olishini tasvirlaydi va Dsup oqsili orqali buning bir sababini ko'rsatadi. Kosmik missiyalar yoki kashfiyot tarixi haqida gap yo'q.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Along the trade routes that crossed Central Asia, caravanserais—roadside inns built around open courtyards—offered merchants shelter, water, and stabling for their camels. Many were spaced roughly a day's journey apart, about 30 to 40 kilometers. Historians once viewed these buildings mainly as places to rest. Recent studies of ruins near Bukhara, however, have uncovered storage rooms, prayer spaces, and even small markets, suggesting that caravanserais also functioned as centers of commerce and cultural exchange.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a type of building, presents an earlier view of its role, and then introduces evidence that expands that view.
It explains how caravanserais were built, then evaluates the materials used to build them.
It compares caravanserais near Bukhara with those elsewhere, then argues that Bukhara's were superior.
It presents a historical debate, then states that the debate cannot be resolved.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn avval karvonsaroyni tasvirlaydi, so'ng tarixchilarning oldingi qarashini keltiradi va nihoyat bu qarashni kengaytiruvchi yangi dalillarni taqdim etadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Marian Ellsworth's 1908 novel The Lamplighter's Daughter. Hattie has just arrived at her aunt's house in the city.
Hattie had imagined the city as a place of glittering shop windows and endless music. [underlined: What she found instead, on that first gray morning, was a narrow street where the rain collected in the gutters and a single cart horse stood patiently beneath a dripping awning.] Still, she pressed her face to the window and watched the horse for a long while, as if it might at any moment reveal some secret the city had been keeping for her alone.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It explains why Hattie decides to leave the city.
It introduces a character who becomes important later in the text.
It describes the interior of the aunt's house in detail.
It contrasts the reality of the city with Hattie's expectations of it.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Birinchi gapda Hattie shaharni yorqin va musiqali deb tasavvur qilgani aytiladi; tagiga chizilgan gap esa haqiqatda kulrang, tor ko'chani ko'rganini bildirib, kutish va haqiqat o'rtasidagi ziddiyatni yaratadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Economists have long observed that people tend to value items more highly once they own them, a tendency known as the endowment effect. In a classic experiment, participants who were given a coffee mug asked, on average, roughly twice as much money to sell it as other participants were willing to pay for the same mug. The finding challenged the assumption that people assign a fixed value to goods regardless of whether they possess them.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that coffee mugs are generally overpriced
To explain a tendency in how people value what they own and describe evidence for it
To criticize economists for relying too heavily on experiments
To describe how prices are set in retail stores
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn "endowment effect" hodisasini tushuntiradi va uni qo'llab-quvvatlovchi krujka tajribasini keltiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Suzani, the large embroidered textiles of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, were traditionally made by women as part of a bride's dowry. Because a single suzani could take years to complete, the work was often divided among female relatives, each stitching a separate strip of cloth that was later joined together. Art historians note that this method sometimes produced slight mismatches in pattern where the strips met. Rather than flaws, however, these irregularities are now valued by collectors as evidence of the collaborative, family-centered process through which each suzani was made.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes an artistic tradition, then argues that the tradition has disappeared.
It describes how a type of textile was made, notes a resulting feature, and explains how that feature is now regarded.
It compares two textile traditions, then explains why one became more popular.
It presents a collector's opinion, then offers evidence that contradicts it.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn so'zana qanday tikilganini tasvirlaydi, bu usul natijasida paydo bo'lgan naqsh nomuvofiqliklarini qayd etadi va ular hozir qanday qadrlanishini tushuntiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Many plants rely on bees for pollination, and biologists long assumed that flowers attract bees mainly through color and scent. In 2013, however, researchers at the University of Bristol found that bumblebees can also detect the weak electric fields surrounding flowers. A flower typically carries a slight negative charge, while a bee flying through the air accumulates a positive one. [underlined: When a bee visits a flower, the flower's charge changes briefly, and the researchers found that bees could sense this change and avoid flowers that had recently been visited by other bees.] The discovery suggests that flowers communicate with pollinators through more channels than scientists had recognized.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It introduces the assumption that the researchers set out to challenge.
It explains why flowers carry a negative electric charge.
It offers a criticism of the researchers' methods.
It provides a specific finding that supports the text's conclusion about how flowers communicate with pollinators.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap asalarilar gulning elektr zaryadi o'zgarishini sezishini ko'rsatuvchi aniq natijani beradi; bu esa oxirgi gapdagi gullar changlatuvchilar bilan ko'proq kanallar orqali "muloqot qiladi" degan xulosani qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Thomas Hale's 1894 poem "The Mill Pond."
Still water holds the willow's shape / As if it feared to let it go; / The swallows dip and do not break / The quiet world that sleeps below. / But when the evening wind comes down / And ripples cross from shore to shore, / The willow shivers into gold / And is a willow nevermore.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To depict how a reflection on still water is disturbed by the wind
To argue that ponds should be protected from development
To describe the daily habits of swallows
To express the speaker's sorrow over the loss of a friend
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: She'r avval tinch suvdagi tol aksini tasvirlaydi, so'ng shamol kelib to'lqinlar bu aksni buzishini ko'rsatadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Sociologist Dilnoza Karimova studied how residents of three apartment blocks in Tashkent used their shared courtyards. She found that courtyards with benches and shade trees were used by residents of all ages throughout the day, while courtyards without such features were used mainly by children in the afternoons. Karimova also found that residents of the better-equipped courtyards reported knowing more of their neighbors by name. She concludes that modest investments in courtyard design may strengthen social ties among neighbors.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that apartment blocks in Tashkent are poorly designed
To compare how children and adults spend their free time
To present a researcher's findings about courtyard design and the conclusion she draws from them
To describe the history of shared courtyards in Central Asian cities
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn Karimovaning hovlilar dizayni haqidagi tadqiqot natijalarini va undan chiqargan xulosasini bayon qiladi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: In 1848, the chemist Louis Pasteur was studying crystals of tartaric acid, a substance found in wine sediment. Under a microscope, he noticed that the crystals came in two forms that were mirror images of each other, like a pair of left and right hands. [underlined: Pasteur carefully separated the two forms by hand, using tweezers, and dissolved each in water.] He found that one solution rotated polarized light to the right and the other to the left. This discovery of molecular "handedness" laid the foundation for the field of stereochemistry.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It states the main conclusion of Pasteur's research.
It explains why tartaric acid is found in wine.
It describes a problem that prevented Pasteur from completing his work.
It describes a step in the process that led to Pasteur's discovery.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap Paster kashfiyotga olib kelgan jarayondagi bir bosqichni — kristallarni ajratib, suvda eritishni tasvirlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Critics often dismiss the detective novels of the 1920s and 1930s as mere puzzles, stories in which characters exist only to be suspects or victims. Such readings, however, overlook how thoroughly these novels register the anxieties of their moment. The country houses in which so many of the murders take place are frequently shown to be in decline, their owners struggling with debt and their servants leaving for factory work. The crime at the center of each novel may be solved by the final chapter, but the social disorder surrounding it rarely is.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To challenge a dismissive view of certain novels by showing that they reflect social concerns of their time
To argue that detective novels of the 1920s and 1930s were more popular than other genres
To explain how authors of detective novels constructed their puzzles
To describe the economic decline of country houses in the early twentieth century
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Muallif detektiv romanlarni "shunchaki jumboq" deb hisoblovchi tanqidchilarga e'tiroz bildirib, ular o'z davrining ijtimoiy xavotirlarini aks ettirishini ko'rsatadi. Qishloq uylarining tanazzuli asosiy maqsad emas, balki dalil sifatida keltirilgan.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Octopuses can change the color and texture of their skin in a fraction of a second, blending into rocks, sand, or coral. Yet most octopus species are thought to be colorblind, possessing only one type of light-sensitive cell in their eyes. How, then, do they match colors they cannot see? One hypothesis holds that their skin itself contains light-detecting proteins called opsins, which might allow it to sense color directly. Another proposes that the unusual U-shaped pupils of octopuses could separate light into different wavelengths, giving the animals a limited form of color perception.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a behavior, explains how that behavior evolved, and then gives an example.
It presents a hypothesis, then provides evidence that disproves it.
It identifies a puzzling contradiction, then presents two possible explanations for it.
It compares octopuses with other animals, then argues that octopuses are the most intelligent.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn sakkizoyoqlar rang ko'rmasa ham rangga moslashishi haqidagi jumboqni qo'yadi va unga ikki ehtimoliy izoh (terining opsinlari va U shaklidagi qorachiq) beradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Eleanor Whitcombe's 1899 novel A Season at Ashford. Mrs. Pell is visiting the home of her late sister.
Everything in the parlor was exactly as Mrs. Pell remembered it: the blue china on the mantel, the clock that ran five minutes slow, the faded rug with its pattern of vines. [underlined: Only the chair by the window, where her sister had always sat with her sewing, had been moved, pushed back against the wall as though someone had wished to make the room forget.] Mrs. Pell stood before it a moment, then quietly drew it back into the light.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It establishes that the parlor has been completely redecorated.
It introduces a detail that departs from the otherwise unchanged room and suggests an attempt to set aside the memory of Mrs. Pell's sister.
It reveals that Mrs. Pell disliked her sister's habits.
It explains why the clock in the parlor runs slow.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Xonadagi hamma narsa o'zgarmagan, faqat opasining kursisi surib qo'yilgan; bu tafsilot kimdir marhuma xotirasini chetga surmoqchi bo'lganiga ishora qiladi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: In the early 2000s, most musicians who wanted to record an album needed the support of a record label. The rise of crowdfunding websites changed this. Artists could now ask fans to contribute money directly, often offering signed copies or concert tickets in return. By 2015, thousands of albums had been funded this way. Some critics warn, though, that crowdfunding favors musicians who already have large followings, making it harder for unknown artists to be heard.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a situation in the past, explains a development that changed it, and then notes a concern about that development.
It presents an argument in favor of record labels, then refutes it.
It lists several ways musicians earn money, then ranks them.
It describes a single musician's career from beginning to end.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn avval o'tmishdagi holatni (yorliqqa bog'liqlik), so'ng uni o'zgartirgan kraudfandingni va oxirida bu haqda tanqidchilarning xavotirini keltiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Once the fourth-largest lake in the world, the Aral Sea began shrinking in the 1960s after the rivers that fed it were diverted to irrigate cotton fields. By the 2010s, its southern portion had largely dried up. The northern portion tells a different story. In 2005, Kazakhstan completed the Kokaral Dam, which prevented water from flowing out of the North Aral Sea into the drying south. Within a few years, the North Aral's water level had risen by several meters, and fish species that had disappeared began to return, allowing local fishing communities to revive.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that cotton farming should be banned in Central Asia
To explain why the Aral Sea was once one of the largest lakes in the world
To describe the engineering challenges involved in building dams
To contrast the decline of the Aral Sea as a whole with the partial recovery of one of its parts
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn Orol dengizining umumiy qurishini Kokaral to'g'oni tufayli Shimoliy Orolning qisman tiklanishi bilan qiyoslaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Henry Calloway's 1912 short story "The Surveyor."
Josiah Merrow had surveyed the valley for thirty years, and he knew it as other men know the faces of their children. He could name the depth of every creek and the age of every oak along the ridge. So when the young engineer from the railroad company unrolled his maps and began to explain where the new line would run, Josiah listened politely. Then he pointed, without a word, to a narrow bend in the river the engineer had marked as solid ground—a place Josiah knew flooded each spring.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a conflict between two characters, then shows how they resolve it through compromise.
It presents Josiah's memories of his childhood, then shifts to a description of the valley's history.
It establishes Josiah's deep knowledge of the valley, then presents a situation in which that knowledge reveals an error.
It describes the construction of a railroad, then explains the damage caused by a flood.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn avval Josiahning vodiyni juda yaxshi bilishini ko'rsatadi, so'ng bu bilim muhandis xaritasidagi xatoni fosh etgan vaziyatni tasvirlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Arctic terns migrate farther than any other animal, traveling from breeding grounds in the Arctic to the coast of Antarctica and back each year. [underlined: Tracking devices attached to terns in Greenland revealed that a single bird can fly more than 70,000 kilometers in one year.] Because terns can live for 30 years, one bird may travel a distance equal to three round trips to the Moon over its lifetime. Scientists believe the birds follow a winding route to take advantage of prevailing winds.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It introduces a question that the rest of the text answers.
It provides evidence supporting the claim made in the first sentence.
It explains why terns follow a winding route.
It presents a view that the text later rejects.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Birinchi gapda qutb qarqunoqlari eng uzoq migratsiya qilishi aytiladi; tagiga chizilgan gap buni aniq raqam (70 000 km) bilan tasdiqlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: In the fifteenth century, Samarkand was home to one of the most advanced observatories in the world. Built by the ruler and astronomer Ulugh Beg in the 1420s, it housed an enormous meridian arc, a curved instrument more than 40 meters long set into a trench in the ground. [underlined: Using this instrument, Ulugh Beg and his colleagues measured the length of the year to within about one minute of the value accepted today.] Their star catalogue, listing the positions of more than a thousand stars, remained a standard reference for astronomers for over two centuries.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It describes how the observatory was constructed.
It explains why the observatory was eventually destroyed.
It gives an example of the precision achieved at the observatory, supporting the claim that it was highly advanced.
It introduces a disagreement between Ulugh Beg and his colleagues.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap yil uzunligining deyarli bir daqiqa aniqlikda o'lchanganini aytadi — bu rasadxona eng ilg'orlardan biri bo'lgani haqidagi da'voni tasdiqlovchi misoldir.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Economists typically measure a country's prosperity using gross domestic product (GDP), the total value of goods and services it produces. Yet GDP counts only activities that involve market transactions. When a parent cooks a meal, cares for an elderly relative, or repairs a leaking faucet, no money changes hands, and none of that labor appears in official statistics. Some estimates suggest that if unpaid household work were valued at market wages, it would equal between 10 and 40 percent of GDP, depending on the country. For this reason, a number of economists have called for supplementary measures that capture this hidden portion of economic life.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To point out a limitation of a common economic measure and note a proposed response to it
To argue that household work should be paid at market wages
To explain how gross domestic product is calculated in different countries
To compare the economies of countries with high and low GDP
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn YaIMning cheklovini (haq to'lanmaydigan uy mehnatini hisobga olmasligini) ko'rsatadi va iqtisodchilar taklif qilgan qo'shimcha o'lchovlarni qayd etadi. Uy mehnatiga haq to'lash taklif qilinmaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Clara Voss's 1903 novel The Harbor Road.
Every morning at six, the ferry sounded its horn twice, and every morning at six, old Mr. Tobin rose from his bed to watch it pass. He did not travel on it; he had not left the island in forty years. Yet he knew each of the ferry's crew by name and would wave to them from his porch, and on the rare days the fog kept the boat in harbor, he seemed restless until evening, as though some small but necessary part of the world had gone missing.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To explain why Mr. Tobin refuses to leave the island
To describe the ferry's route across the harbor
To show how the ferry's crew feels about Mr. Tobin
To portray a character's quiet attachment to a daily routine
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn janob Tobinning har kuni paromni kuzatish odatiga bog'liqligini tasvirlaydi. U nega oroldan chiqmasligi tushuntirilmaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: The Uzbek classical music tradition known as Shashmaqam consists of six suites, or maqams, each built around a distinct set of melodic modes. For centuries, the repertoire was passed down orally from master to student, a process that could take a decade or more. In the 1920s, musicologists began transcribing the pieces into Western notation for the first time. Some performers welcomed the transcriptions as a way to preserve the tradition, but others argued that notation could not capture the subtle ornaments and rhythmic flexibility that give Shashmaqam its character.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It explains the origins of a musical tradition, then describes its influence on Western music.
It describes a musical tradition and how it was transmitted, then presents differing reactions to a change in how it was recorded.
It argues that oral transmission is superior to written notation, then provides examples.
It profiles a famous performer of Shashmaqam and describes his training.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn Shashmaqom an'anasini va uning og'zaki uzatilishini tasvirlaydi, so'ng notaga yozishga ijrochilarning turli munosabatlarini keltiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Sea otters are sometimes called a keystone species because of their outsized influence on the ecosystems they inhabit. Otters eat large quantities of sea urchins, which in turn feed on kelp. [underlined: When otters were hunted nearly to extinction along the Pacific coast in the 1800s and early 1900s, urchin populations exploded, and vast kelp forests were reduced to barren rock.] In areas where otters have since been reintroduced, kelp has rebounded, providing habitat for fish, crabs, and countless other species.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It illustrates the claim about otters' influence by describing what happened when otters were largely removed.
It explains why sea otters were hunted.
It introduces a counterargument to the idea that otters are a keystone species.
It describes the diet of sea urchins in detail.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap dengiz qunduzlari yo'qolganda nima bo'lganini ko'rsatib, ularning ekotizimga katta ta'siri haqidagi da'voni misol bilan tasdiqlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Agnes Marlowe's 1887 poem "To a Stone Wall."
You were raised by hands long gone to dust, / Stone laid on stone without mortar or plan, / And still you stand, though the farmhouse fell / And the fields went back to the fern. / No one remembers who hauled you here / Or what they meant you to keep in or out; / Yet the moss knows every crack of you / And the wren has made you home.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To mourn the destruction of an old farmhouse by a storm
To describe the process of building a stone wall without mortar
To criticize the farmers who abandoned their fields
To reflect on how an old wall endures and gains new purpose after its builders and original use are forgotten
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: She'r quruvchilari va asl vazifasi unutilgan devorning hanuz turganini, endi mox va chittak uchun uy bo'lganini aks ettiradi. Bo'ron yoki fermerlarni tanqid qilish haqida gap yo'q.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Volcanic eruptions can affect the climate of the entire planet. When Mount Tambora in Indonesia erupted in 1815, it released enormous amounts of sulfur dioxide into the upper atmosphere, where the gas formed tiny droplets that reflected sunlight back into space. The following year became known in Europe and North America as "the year without a summer." Snow fell in New England in June, and crop failures led to food shortages across several continents.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a scientific debate, then offers a resolution to it.
It makes a general claim, then supports it with a specific historical example.
It presents a series of eruptions in chronological order.
It explains how volcanoes form, then describes their effects on nearby towns.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn umumiy da'vo (vulqonlar butun sayyora iqlimiga ta'sir qiladi) bilan boshlanadi va uni Tambora otilishi misoli bilan qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Linguists have observed that bilingual speakers often switch between languages in the middle of a conversation, or even a single sentence, a practice known as code-switching. Code-switching was once widely viewed as a sign that speakers lacked full command of either language. Research over the past several decades, however, has shown that code-switching follows consistent grammatical rules and is most common among speakers who are highly proficient in both languages. Many speakers use it deliberately, for example to express a feeling that one language captures better than the other.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that everyone should learn a second language
To describe how children acquire two languages at once
To present research that challenges an earlier negative view of a linguistic practice
To explain the grammatical rules of a particular language
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn kod almashtirish ilgari til bilmaslik belgisi deb hisoblanganini, so'nggi tadqiqotlar esa buning aksini ko'rsatganini bayon qiladi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Photography was invented in the 1830s, and for decades afterward many painters feared it would make their art obsolete. Why paint a portrait, they asked, when a camera could produce a perfect likeness in minutes? [underlined: Yet some artists came to see the camera not as a rival but as a liberation.] Freed from the obligation to record appearances precisely, painters such as Claude Monet and Edgar Degas turned their attention to fleeting effects of light, unusual angles, and subjective impressions—qualities the cameras of their day could not capture.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It restates the painters' fears described earlier in the text.
It provides evidence that photography was more popular than painting.
It introduces a criticism of Monet's and Degas's work.
It marks a shift from describing a fear about photography to presenting a more positive response to it.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: "Yet" bilan boshlangan gap rassomlarning fotografiyadan qo'rquvidan unga ijobiy munosabatga — uni ozodlik deb ko'rishga o'tishni belgilaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Some desert beetles have a remarkable way of collecting water. The Namib Desert beetle, which lives in one of the driest places on Earth, climbs to the top of sand dunes on foggy mornings and tilts its body into the wind. Tiny droplets of fog collect on bumps on its back, grow larger, and roll down grooves into the beetle's mouth. Engineers have studied the beetle's shell to design materials that can harvest drinking water from fog.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that deserts are expanding because of climate change
To compare several species of desert beetles
To explain how a beetle gathers water and note how its method has inspired engineers
To describe the weather patterns of the Namib Desert
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn Namib qo'ng'izi tumandan suv yig'ish usulini tushuntiradi va muhandislar bundan ilhomlanganini qayd etadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Nathaniel Brooke's 1874 novel The Winter Ledger.
Amos Grey had kept the accounts of the general store for twenty years without a single error. Each evening he recorded the day's sales in a neat, narrow hand, blotted the page, and locked the ledger in the drawer beneath the counter. But on the night of the first snow, he found a figure he could not explain—a sum of eleven dollars paid for goods that no one, so far as he could recall, had ever purchased. He sat for a long time with his pen above the page.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It establishes a character's careful habits, then introduces an unexpected problem that disrupts them.
It describes a store's history, then explains why the store closed.
It presents a conversation between two characters, then describes its consequences.
It describes a snowstorm, then shifts to the character's memories of childhood.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn avval Amosning yigirma yil xatosiz hisob yuritish odatini ko'rsatadi, so'ng bu tartibni buzuvchi tushunarsiz summani kiritadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: For decades, astronomers assumed that planets could form only around single stars like the Sun. In a binary system, where two stars orbit each other, the gravitational pull of the companion star was expected to disrupt the disk of gas and dust from which planets form. [underlined: In 2011, however, NASA's Kepler space telescope detected Kepler-16b, a planet orbiting both stars of a binary system.] Since then, more than a dozen such "circumbinary" planets have been confirmed, and some researchers now estimate that they may be fairly common in our galaxy.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It explains why the companion star disrupts planet formation.
It presents a discovery that contradicts the assumption described earlier in the text.
It provides an example that supports the astronomers' original assumption.
It introduces the main question that the text leaves unanswered.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap ikki yulduz atrofida aylanuvchi sayyora kashf etilganini aytadi va bu avvalgi "sayyoralar faqat yakka yulduz atrofida hosil bo'ladi" degan taxminni rad etadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Papermaking was invented in China around the second century CE, and for centuries the technique remained largely unknown outside East Asia. [underlined: According to a widely repeated account, the craft reached the Islamic world in 751, when Chinese papermakers captured at the Battle of Talas were brought to Samarkand.] Whether or not that story is accurate, Samarkand soon became famous for its high-quality paper, and from there the technique spread to Baghdad, Cairo, and eventually Europe, where it transformed the production of books.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It offers a traditional explanation of how papermaking spread beyond East Asia.
It argues that papermaking was invented in Samarkand.
It describes the materials used to make paper.
It explains why Europe was slow to adopt paper.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap qog'oz ishlab chiqarish Sharqiy Osiyodan tashqariga qanday tarqalgani haqidagi keng tarqalgan rivoyatni keltiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: In a study of more than 2,000 households, economist Priya Menon examined how families in rural India spent unexpected income, such as cash transfers or harvest windfalls. Standard economic models predicted that families would spend most of the money on immediate consumption. Menon found instead that a majority of households invested the funds in livestock, tools, or school fees for their children—choices likely to increase their earnings over time. Her results suggest that low-income families may plan for the future more than the models assumed.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that cash transfers should replace other forms of aid
To present a study whose findings run counter to a prediction of standard economic models
To describe the daily life of families in rural India
To explain why livestock is a valuable investment
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn Menon tadqiqotini taqdim etadi: modellar oilalar pulni darhol sarflaydi deb bashorat qilgan, ammo natijalar buning aksini ko'rsatgan.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Scholars of the Renaissance have traditionally credited a handful of Italian masters with the invention of linear perspective, the technique that allows painters to create the illusion of depth on a flat surface. Filippo Brunelleschi's experiments in Florence around 1415 are usually cited as the decisive moment. Yet art historian Hana Lindqvist argues that this account is too narrow. She points to earlier optical treatises by the Arab scholar Ibn al-Haytham, whose work on vision was translated into Latin in the thirteenth century. Brunelleschi's achievement, Lindqvist contends, drew on a long, international conversation about vision and space.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a technique, explains how it works, then gives examples of paintings that use it.
It presents two scholars' views, then concludes that neither is correct.
It traces the career of an artist from his training to his most famous works.
It presents a traditional account of an artistic development, then describes a scholar's argument that the account overlooks important influences.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn avval chiziqli perspektiva kashfiyoti haqidagi an'anaviy qarashni beradi, so'ng Lindqvistning bu qarash muhim ta'sirlarni (Ibn al-Haysam) e'tiborsiz qoldirgani haqidagi dalilini keltiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Why do leaves change color in the fall? During spring and summer, leaves are green because they contain large amounts of chlorophyll, the pigment plants use to capture sunlight. Leaves also contain yellow and orange pigments, but these are hidden by the chlorophyll. As days shorten in autumn, trees stop producing chlorophyll, and the green fades. The yellow and orange pigments, present all along, finally become visible.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes an experiment, then presents its results.
It presents two competing theories, then argues for one of them.
It poses a question, then provides an explanation that answers it.
It describes a tree's life cycle from seed to maturity.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn savol bilan boshlanadi (barglar nega rangini o'zgartiradi?) va keyin unga javob beruvchi izohni beradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Rosalind Ashby's 1896 novel The Tenants of Mill Street. Lucy, a young seamstress, has just been offered a position in a fashionable shop.
Lucy read the letter three times before she let herself believe it. A position at Delacroix's! She thought of the shop's tall windows and the ladies in silk who swept in and out of its doors. [underlined: Then her eyes fell on her mother's thin hands, busy with the mending by the fire, and the letter grew suddenly heavy in her own.] To accept would mean leaving the house before dawn and returning long after dark.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It reveals that Lucy's mother wrote the letter.
It introduces a concern that tempers Lucy's excitement about the offer.
It describes the shop where Lucy hopes to work.
It shows that Lucy has already decided to reject the offer.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Lucy avval xursand bo'ladi, ammo onasining ozg'in qo'llarini ko'rgach, xat "og'irlashadi" — bu uning quvonchini susaytiruvchi xavotirni kiritadi. U taklifni rad etishga qaror qilgani aytilmaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Most people assume that the ocean's deepest regions are nearly lifeless, too cold and dark to support much activity. In 1977, however, scientists aboard the submersible Alvin discovered hydrothermal vents on the floor of the Pacific Ocean, where superheated, mineral-rich water pours from cracks in the seabed. Surrounding the vents were dense communities of giant tube worms, clams, and crabs. These animals depend not on sunlight but on bacteria that convert chemicals from the vents into energy, a process called chemosynthesis. The discovery revealed that entire ecosystems can exist independent of the Sun.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To describe a discovery that overturned a common assumption about life in the deep ocean
To explain how the submersible Alvin was designed
To argue that more funding should go to ocean exploration
To compare chemosynthesis and photosynthesis in detail
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn okean tubi deyarli jonsiz degan keng tarqalgan taxminni rad etgan gidrotermal manbalar kashfiyotini tasvirlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: For decades, a stream called Cheonggyecheon ran beneath an elevated highway in the center of Seoul, South Korea, hidden from view. In 2003, city officials made the controversial decision to demolish the highway and restore the stream. Critics predicted traffic chaos. Instead, after the project was completed in 2005, traffic in the area adjusted as drivers found other routes or switched to public transit. The restored stream now attracts tens of thousands of visitors a day, and studies have found that summer temperatures along its banks are several degrees cooler than on nearby streets.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes the construction of a highway, then explains why the highway became congested.
It compares two cities' approaches to urban planning.
It describes a controversial decision, notes a prediction about its effects, and then explains that the actual outcome differed from that prediction.
It argues that all highways in large cities should be replaced by parks.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn munozarali qarorni, tanqidchilarning transport tartibsizligi haqidagi bashoratini va haqiqiy natija boshqacha bo'lganini ketma-ket bayon qiladi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: In 1903, Marie Curie became the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, sharing the award in physics with her husband, Pierre, and Henri Becquerel for their research on radioactivity. Eight years later, she won a second Nobel Prize, this time in chemistry, for discovering the elements polonium and radium. Curie named polonium after Poland, the country of her birth. She remains the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To explain how radioactivity was first discovered
To argue that the Nobel Prize should be awarded more often to women
To describe Pierre Curie's contributions to physics
To highlight Marie Curie's distinctive scientific achievements
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn Mari Kyuri yutuqlarining o'ziga xosligini — birinchi ayol laureat va ikki xil fanda mukofot olgan yagona inson ekanini ta'kidlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Walter Penrose's 1901 poem "The Old Clockmaker."
He mended hours for sixty years, / Set springs and gears in patient rows, / And every clock along the lane / Kept time because his hands were close. / [underlined: But no one mended his own days,] / Which slipped like water through the town; / And when at last his shop fell still, / The clocks ticked on without him there.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It describes the tools the clockmaker used in his work.
It suggests that the townspeople disliked the clockmaker.
It reinforces the idea that the clockmaker's work was admired.
It introduces a contrast between the clockmaker's care for others' clocks and the passing of his own life.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: "But" bilan boshlangan satr soatsozning boshqalar soatini tuzatganini uning o'z umri esa hech kim tomonidan "tuzatilmay" o'tib ketgani bilan qarama-qarshi qo'yadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Psychologists have long studied the "bystander effect," the tendency of individuals to be less likely to help someone in need when other people are present. Early studies, conducted mostly in laboratories, suggested the effect was strong. However, a 2019 analysis of more than 200 real-world conflicts recorded by public security cameras in three countries found that in about 90 percent of cases, at least one bystander intervened to help. The researchers suggest that larger groups may actually increase the chance that someone will step forward.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To present real-world findings that complicate an idea based on earlier laboratory studies
To explain why people refuse to help strangers
To describe how security cameras are used by police
To argue that laboratory studies are always unreliable
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn laboratoriya tadqiqotlariga asoslangan "kuzatuvchi effekti" g'oyasini murakkablashtiruvchi real hayotdagi natijalarni taqdim etadi. "Har doim ishonchsiz" degan da'vo juda kuchli.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: The Himalayas, home to Mount Everest, are still rising. The mountain range formed when the Indian tectonic plate collided with the Eurasian plate about 50 million years ago. [underlined: That collision has never fully stopped: the Indian plate continues to push northward at a rate of about 5 centimeters per year.] As a result, the Himalayas gain a few millimeters in height each year, though erosion from wind, rain, and glaciers wears some of that height away.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It states the current height of Mount Everest.
It explains why the Himalayas are still rising, as stated at the beginning of the text.
It presents a theory that the text later disproves.
It compares the Himalayas with other mountain ranges.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap Hind plitasi hali ham shimolga surilayotganini aytib, birinchi gapdagi Himoloy hali ham ko'tarilmoqda degan fikrni tushuntiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: The eleventh-century scholar Ibn Sina, known in Europe as Avicenna, proposed a thought experiment now called the "Floating Man." Imagine, he wrote, a person created fully formed but suspended in the air, blindfolded, with limbs spread apart so that they touch nothing, not even each other. Such a person would receive no information from the senses. Would that person still be aware of his own existence? Ibn Sina answered yes, and he concluded that self-awareness does not depend on the body or the senses. Later philosophers, including René Descartes, would explore strikingly similar ideas.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It presents an argument, then lists the criticisms other philosophers made of it.
It describes Ibn Sina's life, then summarizes his medical writings.
It introduces a thought experiment, describes it, presents the conclusion its author drew, and notes later echoes of it.
It compares two philosophers, then argues that Descartes's ideas were more original.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn "Muallaq odam" tajribasini tanishtiradi, uni tasvirlaydi, Ibn Sino chiqargan xulosani beradi va keyingi faylasuflardagi aks-sadosini qayd etadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Margaret Fenwick's 1910 novel The House at Wren's End. The narrator describes her grandmother.
My grandmother never spoke of the war, and we children learned early not to ask. But every autumn she planted tulip bulbs along the garden wall—exactly forty of them, never more or fewer—and every spring, when they bloomed, she would walk the length of the wall slowly, touching each flower as if counting. Once I asked why forty. She looked at me for a long moment, then said only that it was the number she had promised.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To explain the narrator's grandmother's role during the war
To suggest, through a character's ritual, a significance in her past that she does not openly discuss
To describe how to plant and care for tulip bulbs
To show the narrator's frustration with her grandmother's secrecy
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Buvining har yili aynan qirqta lola ekish odati u gapirmaydigan o'tmishdagi muhim voqeaga ishora qiladi. Uning urushdagi roli ochiq tushuntirilmaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Biologists have long debated why zebras have stripes. Proposed explanations include camouflage, temperature regulation, and social recognition. A series of field experiments in the 2010s tested a less obvious idea: that stripes deter biting flies. Researchers dressed horses in striped, black, and white coats and filmed flies approaching them. [underlined: Flies circled and touched the striped coats as often as the others but landed on them far less frequently, apparently failing to slow down properly before contact.] The researchers concluded that stripes may interfere with flies' visual systems, protecting zebras from insects that transmit disease.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It presents the hypothesis that the researchers set out to test.
It describes a flaw in the design of the experiment.
It presents the key observation on which the researchers based their conclusion.
It explains why other proposed explanations for stripes are incorrect.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap tajribaning asosiy kuzatuvini beradi: pashshalar yo'l-yo'l choponlarga kamroq qo'nadi. Tadqiqotchilarning xulosasi aynan shu kuzatuvga asoslangan.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: In arid regions of Iran and Central Asia, ancient engineers developed an ingenious method of supplying water to farms and towns: the qanat, or karez. A qanat is a gently sloping underground tunnel that carries groundwater from the foot of a mountain to fields many kilometers away. Because the water travels underground, little of it is lost to evaporation. Some qanats built more than a thousand years ago still function today. In recent decades, however, many have fallen into disuse as farmers have turned to electric pumps, which draw water faster but have lowered groundwater levels in some areas.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes an ancient technology and its advantages, then notes a recent change that threatens it.
It argues that electric pumps are superior to older technologies.
It explains how groundwater forms beneath mountains.
It compares qanats in Iran with those in Central Asia.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn qadimiy kariz texnologiyasi va uning afzalliklarini tasvirlaydi, so'ng elektr nasoslarga o'tish uni xavf ostiga qo'yayotganini qayd etadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Hummingbirds have the fastest metabolism of any bird. To fuel their rapid wingbeats—up to 80 per second in some species—they must eat roughly half their body weight in sugar each day. At night, when they cannot feed, many hummingbirds enter a state called torpor, lowering their body temperature and slowing their heart rate dramatically. This allows them to save energy until morning, when they can feed again.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To compare hummingbirds with other birds that migrate
To argue that people should plant flowers for hummingbirds
To describe the different colors of hummingbird feathers
To explain how hummingbirds meet and conserve their high energy needs
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn kolibrilar yuqori energiya ehtiyojini qanday qondirishi (ko'p shakar iste'mol qilish) va tunda uni qanday tejashini (torpor) tushuntiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Many people believe that multitasking helps them get more done. [underlined: Research suggests otherwise.] In one study, participants who switched frequently between tasks took significantly longer to complete them and made more errors than participants who focused on one task at a time. Psychologists explain that the brain does not truly perform two demanding tasks simultaneously; instead, it rapidly shifts attention back and forth, losing time and accuracy with each shift.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It signals that the text will challenge the belief stated in the first sentence.
It summarizes the results of a single study in detail.
It introduces a new belief that the text goes on to support.
It explains how the brain shifts attention between tasks.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Qisqa gap "tadqiqotlar boshqacha ko'rsatadi" deb, matn birinchi gapdagi ko'p vazifalilik haqidagi e'tiqodga qarshi chiqishini bildiradi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Architect Farhod Usmonov designed the new public library in Namangan with an unusual feature: its reading rooms have no windows facing the street. Instead, every room looks onto a central courtyard planted with pomegranate and mulberry trees. Some residents initially criticized the design as closed-off and unwelcoming. Usmonov responded that he had drawn on the tradition of the Central Asian courtyard house, in which rooms turn inward to create a sheltered, quiet space away from the noise of the street—exactly the atmosphere, he argued, that a library should provide.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that all libraries should be built without windows
To describe an unusual architectural choice and the reasoning its designer offered for it
To explain how pomegranate trees are cultivated in courtyards
To report residents' complaints about a public building
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn kutubxonaning g'ayrioddiy dizaynini va me'mor Usmonovning bu tanlov uchun keltirgan asosini tasvirlaydi. Aholining tanqidi faqat bir qism, asosiy maqsad emas.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Oliver Pryce's 1885 novel The Keeper's Son.
At dawn the lighthouse was only a gray shape against a gray sea. By midmorning the fog had lifted, and the white tower gleamed so brightly that the fishermen shaded their eyes as they passed. And at dusk, when young Tom climbed the winding stairs to light the great lamp, the tower seemed to him less a building than a living thing, waking to keep watch through the long night.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a conversation between Tom and the fishermen.
It explains how the lighthouse lamp works.
It describes the lighthouse at different times of day, ending with Tom's view of it.
It tells the story of how the lighthouse was built.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn mayoqni tong, tush oldi va shom paytida tasvirlaydi hamda Tomning unga bo'lgan tasavvuri bilan yakunlanadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Caffeine is usually thought of as a stimulant for humans, but for the plants that produce it, it serves a different purpose. In high concentrations, caffeine is toxic to many insects, protecting coffee and tea leaves from being eaten. [underlined: Surprisingly, the nectar of some coffee and citrus flowers contains small amounts of caffeine as well.] Researchers found that bees that fed on caffeinated nectar were three times more likely to remember the flower's scent than bees that fed on nectar without caffeine, suggesting that the plants may use low doses of caffeine to encourage pollinators to return.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It restates the claim that caffeine protects plants from insects.
It explains why humans consume caffeine.
It describes a flaw in the researchers' experiment.
It introduces an unexpected fact that leads to the discussion of a second role caffeine may play for plants.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tagiga chizilgan gap nektarda ham kofein borligi haqidagi kutilmagan faktni keltiradi va bu kofeinning o'simliklar uchun ikkinchi vazifasi — changlatuvchilarni qaytarishga oid muhokamaga yo'l ochadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Historians frequently describe the spread of the printing press in fifteenth-century Europe as a revolution that rapidly democratized knowledge. Historian Beatrice Lang urges caution. She notes that in 1500, most Europeans could not read, and printed books remained expensive enough that ownership was largely limited to clergy, scholars, and wealthy merchants. For most people, Lang argues, the effects of print arrived slowly and indirectly—through sermons, public readings, and inexpensive pamphlets—over the course of more than a century.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that the printing press had no effect on European society
To explain how the first printing presses operated
To present a historian's view that qualifies a common characterization of the printing press's impact
To describe the reading habits of fifteenth-century clergy
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Lang bosmaxona ta'sirini inkor etmaydi, balki uning bilimni "tez" demokratlashtirgani haqidagi keng tarqalgan tavsifni cheklaydi: ta'sir sekin va bilvosita bo'lgan.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Scientists have long known that sleep helps people remember what they learned during the day, but how it does so has been less clear. One leading explanation focuses on brief bursts of brain activity called sleep spindles. In a 2020 study, researchers recorded the brain activity of volunteers who had memorized word pairs before a nap. Volunteers who produced more sleep spindles during the nap recalled significantly more word pairs afterward. The findings support the idea that spindles help transfer memories into long-term storage, though the researchers note that more work is needed.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a common belief about sleep, then shows that belief to be false.
It compares two theories of memory, then rejects both of them.
It presents a series of tips for improving memory.
It identifies an open question, introduces one possible explanation, and describes a study that supports it.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn ochiq savolni (uyqu xotiraga qanday yordam beradi?) qo'yadi, bir izohni (uyqu shpindellari) kiritadi va uni qo'llab-quvvatlovchi tadqiqotni tasvirlaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from Isabel Thorne's 1892 novel Meadowcroft. Mr. Harlow is a wealthy landowner.
Mr. Harlow liked to say that he had never refused a neighbor in need, and indeed his generosity was spoken of in every parlor in the county. He gave handsomely to the church, sent baskets to the poor at Christmas, and paid for the new roof on the schoolhouse. [underlined: It was only his tenants, who paid him rent each quarter-day, who seemed never to have heard of his generosity at all.] Their cottages had not been repaired in a decade.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It provides further evidence of Mr. Harlow's kindness.
It introduces an ironic contrast that undercuts Mr. Harlow's reputation for generosity.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: The snow leopard, which lives in the mountains of Central and South Asia, is so elusive that it has been called the "ghost of the mountains." Because the cats are rarely seen, estimating their numbers has long been difficult. In recent years, researchers in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan have placed hundreds of motion-activated cameras along rocky ridges where snow leopards travel. Each cat's spot pattern is unique, allowing scientists to identify individuals from photographs and produce more reliable population estimates than were previously possible.

Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn qor qoplonlarini sanashdagi qiyinchilikni va kameralar yordamida uni yengish usulini tushuntiradi.

About 240 athletes from 14 nations competed in 43 events, including track and field, swimming, and wrestling. All of the competitors were men. Over the following century, the Games grew dramatically. Women first competed in 1900, and by the 2020 Tokyo Games, more than 11,000 athletes from over 200 nations took part in 339 events.

Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn birinchi zamonaviy Olimpiada o'yinlarini tasvirlaydi, so'ng o'yinlar vaqt o'tishi bilan qanday kengayganini ko'rsatadi.

The platform hums with a hundred goodbyes, / With trunks and whistles and hurrying feet; / The porters shout and the pigeons rise, / And steam rolls out to the crowded street. / But I stand still where you stood last, / And hear, beneath the engine's roar, / Only the silence you have left— / One voice the station holds no more.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Urban planners once assumed that widening roads would reduce traffic congestion. [underlined: Decades of data, however, point to a phenomenon known as induced demand.] When a road is widened, driving on it becomes temporarily faster, which encourages more people to drive, to drive more often, or to take routes they previously avoided. Within a few years, traffic on the widened road typically returns to its earlier levels—or exceeds them. For this reason, many planners now favor investing in public transit and cycling infrastructure instead.

In Uzbekistan, families prepare sumalak, a sweet paste made from sprouted wheat that is cooked in a large cauldron for up to 24 hours. Text Structure and Purpose.passage: The discovery of penicillin in 1928 is often told as a story of lucky accident. Alexander Fleming, returning from vacation, noticed that mold had contaminated one of his bacterial cultures—and that the bacteria around the mold had died. [underlined: But luck alone would not have been enough: many researchers before Fleming had likely seen similar contamination and simply discarded the spoiled dishes.] What set Fleming apart was his willingness to treat an apparent mistake as a question worth investigating. Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Evolution is often imagined as a process too slow to observe within a human lifetime. Studies of urban wildlife suggest otherwise. In New York City, researchers have documented white-footed mice with genetic changes that may help them digest the fatty foods common in human garbage, and in Puerto Rico, lizards living in cities have evolved stickier toe pads for gripping smooth walls and windows. Green roofs are ineffective and should be removed from dense urban areas.
Green roofs lower street temperatures more in dense neighborhoods than elsewhere.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Yashil tomlar binolarni sovutadi, lekin ko'cha darajasida kam ta'sir qiladi; shuning uchun ular daraxtlar o'rnini bosmasligi kerak.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from Charles Dickens's 1861 novel Great Expectations. The narrator, Pip, recalls returning to his childhood home after years in London.
I had believed that when I came back I should find everything grown smaller, and so it was; but I had not expected to find myself grown smaller too. The forge, the marshes, the church, all looked as they had; it was I who had changed, and the change, I now saw, had not been entirely for the better.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Pip notices that the forge and the church have been rebuilt.
Returning home makes Pip realize that he himself has changed, and not always in positive ways.
Pip is disappointed that his childhood home has been torn down.
Pip is pleased to see that London has improved his character.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Pip uyi o'zgarmaganini, balki o'zi o'zgarganini va bu o'zgarish har doim ham yaxshi bo'lmaganini tushunadi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from Sarah Orne Jewett's 1896 novel The Country of the Pointed Firs. The narrator describes Mrs. Todd, an herbalist in a small coastal town.
Mrs. Todd's garden was small, but every plant in it had a purpose. Some were for tea and some for healing, and a few grew there, she admitted, only because they had belonged to her mother. Neighbors came to her door at all hours, and she would step among the rows with a lantern, choosing leaves for them as carefully as a doctor chooses medicine.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best describes Mrs. Todd as presented in the text?
choices: She is an inexperienced gardener who is still learning which plants are useful.
She is a former doctor who has retired to a coastal town.
She is a private woman who resents neighbors visiting her at night.
She is a knowledgeable, dependable figure whose garden serves both her community and her personal memories.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Mrs. Todd qo'shnilarga istalgan vaqtda yordam beradi va ba'zi o'simliklarni onasining xotirasi uchun saqlaydi. Bu uning bilimli va ishonchli ekanini ko'rsatadi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from Frances Hodgson Burnett's 1911 novel The Secret Garden. Mary, a lonely and ill-tempered girl, has begun secretly tending a neglected garden.
Mary had worked in her garden until it was past noon. She had been so busy that she forgot to feel cross. She found herself wanting to see how the green points had grown by tomorrow, and the day after, and the day after that. Somewhere inside her something that had been shut up tightly was slowly beginning to open, like the buds beneath the dead leaves.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Mary plans to show the garden to everyone in the house.
Mary is disappointed that the garden grows so slowly.
Mary works in the garden only because she has been ordered to.
Caring for the garden begins to change Mary, making her more hopeful and less unhappy.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Bog' bilan shug'ullanish Maryamni o'zgartiradi: u g'azabni unutadi va kelajakni intiqlik bilan kutadi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: In the 1950s, textile artist Anni Albers began producing what she called "pictorial weavings": small, framed textiles meant to hang on walls like paintings rather than to serve as rugs or curtains. At the time, many critics dismissed weaving as a craft rather than a fine art. Albers argued that the grid of warp and weft threads was not a limitation but a structure as expressive as a painter's brushstroke. Her pictorial weavings, which were later exhibited in major museums, helped persuade audiences that textiles could be judged by the same standards as other art forms.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Albers's pictorial weavings challenged the view that weaving was merely a craft and not a fine art.
Critics in the 1950s praised weaving as the most expressive art form.
Albers stopped making practical textiles such as rugs and curtains after the 1950s.
Albers preferred painting to weaving but found weaving more profitable.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Matnning asosiy g'oyasi: Albersning asarlari to'qimachilik ham tasviriy san'at bo'la olishini isbotlashga yordam bergan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Sloths move so slowly that algae grow in their fur, giving them a greenish tint. Scientists have found that this is not simply a sign of laziness. The green color helps sloths blend in with the leaves of the rainforest canopy, making them harder for predators such as eagles to spot. Some researchers also think sloths may eat small amounts of the algae as an extra source of nutrients.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: According to the text, how does algae in their fur benefit sloths?
choices: It warns predators that sloths are poisonous.
It allows them to move more quickly through trees.
It keeps their fur dry during heavy rain.
It helps them stay hidden from predators among leaves.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Yashil suvo'tlar yalqovlarni barglar orasida yashirib, yirtqichlardan himoya qiladi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from Jane Austen's 1817 novel Persuasion. Anne Elliot, who ended her engagement to Captain Wentworth years earlier on the advice of a family friend, reflects on that decision.
She was persuaded that, under every disadvantage of disapprobation at home, and every anxiety attending his profession, she should yet have been a happier woman in maintaining the engagement than she had been in the sacrifice of it. She had been forced into prudence in her youth; she learned romance as she grew older.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best describes Anne's attitude toward her past decision?
choices: She now believes that breaking off the engagement was a mistake.
She thinks Captain Wentworth's profession made him an unsuitable partner.
She believes caution is always wiser than following one's feelings.
She is grateful to her family friend for protecting her from an unwise marriage.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Anna unashuvni saqlab qolganida baxtliroq bo'lishiga ishonadi, ya'ni o'z qarorini xato deb biladi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from Nathaniel Hawthorne's 1850 novel The Scarlet Letter. Hester Prynne has been forced to wear a scarlet letter A as a mark of public shame.
The scarlet letter had not done its office. Hester had in her nature a rich, voluptuous characteristic—a taste for the gorgeously beautiful—which found expression in the delicate needlework with which she embroidered the letter itself. What was meant to humble her, she had made into an object of such artistry that it seemed to set her apart rather than bring her low.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Hester transforms a symbol meant to shame her into an expression of her own artistic nature.
Hester accepts the punishment and becomes ashamed of her talents.
Hester sells her needlework to pay for her crimes.
Hester hides the scarlet letter so that no one will notice it.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Hester sharmandalik belgisini o'z badiiy iste'dodining ifodasiga aylantiradi, shuning uchun u o'z vazifasini bajarmagan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth; some species can grow nearly a meter in a single day. Because it regrows quickly after being cut and needs little fertilizer, builders in countries such as Colombia and Indonesia increasingly use bamboo in place of wood and steel. Engineers note that bamboo is also surprisingly strong for its weight, making it useful for floors, walls, and even bridges.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: According to the text, why are builders increasingly using bamboo?
choices: It is cheaper to import than local wood.
It grows only in Colombia and Indonesia.
It is heavier and more rigid than steel.
It regrows quickly, needs little fertilizer, and is strong for its weight.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Matnda bambuk tez qayta o'sishi, kam o'g'it talab qilishi va vazniga nisbatan mustahkamligi aytilgan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Glass frogs, found in the rainforests of Central and South America, get their name from the transparent skin on their bellies, through which their hearts and other organs can be seen. Scientists recently discovered that when glass frogs sleep, they hide most of their red blood cells in their livers. This makes their bodies even more transparent, helping them blend into the green leaves where they rest during the day.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: According to the text, why do glass frogs hide red blood cells in their livers while sleeping?
choices: It changes their skin color from green to red.
It keeps their hearts from working too hard at night.
It helps them digest food more efficiently.
It makes them more transparent and harder to see against leaves.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Qon hujayralarini jigarda yashirish ularni yanada shaffof qilib, barglar orasida ko'rinmas bo'lishga yordam beradi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from L. M. Montgomery's 1908 novel Anne of Green Gables. Anne, an orphan girl, has just arrived at her new home.
"Isn't it splendid to think of all the things there are to find out about? It just makes me feel glad to be alive—it's such an interesting world. It wouldn't be half so interesting if we knew all about everything, would it? There'd be no scope for imagination then, would there?"
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best describes Anne as presented in the text?
choices: She is frustrated that she does not know more about the world.
She is anxious about living in an unfamiliar place.
She is curious and enthusiastic about discovering new things.
She is bored by the questions other people ask her.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Anne dunyoni o'rganish imkoniyatidan xursand: "it's such an interesting world". Bu uning qiziquvchan va g'ayratli ekanini ko'rsatadi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Historian Farida Yusupova studied the caravanserais—roadside inns—that lined the Silk Road trade routes through Central Asia. These buildings offered travelers shelter, water, and a secure courtyard for camels and goods. Yusupova argues that caravanserais were more than rest stops: because merchants from many regions gathered there, they became places where languages, religious ideas, recipes, and technologies were exchanged.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Yusupova argues that the Silk Road was less important than historians believe.
Yusupova claims that caravanserais were built mainly to house camels.
Yusupova argues that Silk Road caravanserais served as important centers of cultural exchange, not just places to rest.
Yusupova shows that few merchants actually used the caravanserais.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Yusupovaning fikricha, karvonsaroylar faqat dam olish joyi emas, madaniy almashinuv markazlari ham bo'lgan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: In a poem by the invented poet Tomasz Wierzbicki, the speaker describes his mother's handwritten recipe cards, stained with oil and softened by years of use. The speaker admits that he cannot follow the recipes exactly, because his mother never wrote down amounts, only phrases like "enough flour" and "until it looks right." Rather than frustrating him, these vague instructions make the speaker feel that his mother is still guiding him, trusting him to learn by feel as she did.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best describes the speaker's view of the recipe cards?
choices: He is annoyed that the cards are too damaged to read.
He wishes his mother had included exact measurements.
He treasures them because their imprecise directions make him feel connected to his mother.
He plans to rewrite the recipes so others can follow them.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Aniq o'lchovlarsiz yozilgan retseptlar uni asabiylashtirmaydi, aksincha onasi hali ham unga yo'l ko'rsatayotgandek his qildiradi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Every spring, thousands of volunteers in the Netherlands help toads cross roads safely. Toads migrate at night from the woods where they spend the winter to ponds where they lay their eggs, and many are killed by cars along the way. Volunteers set up low fences beside busy roads, collect the toads in buckets, and carry them to the other side. In some towns, officials have also built small tunnels under roads so the animals can cross on their own.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Dutch officials have banned driving at night in the spring.
People in the Netherlands use several methods to protect migrating toads from traffic.
Volunteers raise toads in buckets until they are fully grown.
Toads in the Netherlands spend the winter in ponds.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Matnning asosiy g'oyasi — Niderlandiyada qurbaqalarni mashinalardan himoya qilish uchun turli usullar qo'llaniladi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Economists have long assumed that people who win lotteries quickly spend their winnings and return to their previous financial situation. A study of Swedish lottery winners by a team led by Erik Lindqvist complicates that picture. Tracking thousands of winners for up to two decades, the researchers found that most winners did not squander their prizes; instead, they reduced their working hours modestly and saved a substantial share of the money. The researchers note, however, that Swedish winners typically receive prizes in smaller amounts than the enormous jackpots publicized in some other countries, which may shape how winners behave.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Most lottery winners around the world save the majority of their winnings.
Economists have proven that large jackpots cause winners to spend recklessly.
A long-term study of Swedish lottery winners challenges a common assumption about winners' spending, though the findings may reflect features specific to Sweden's prizes.
Lottery winners in Sweden tend to quit their jobs entirely and live on their savings.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Tadqiqot odatiy taxminni shubha ostiga qo'yadi, ammo mualliflar natijalar Shvetsiyadagi kichikroq yutuqlarga bog'liq bo'lishi mumkinligini ham qayd etadi. Boshqa variantlar haddan tashqari umumlashtirilgan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: In a poem by the invented poet Celeste Arnaud, the speaker walks through the house where she grew up, now empty and for sale. She describes each room in precise detail—the height marks on a doorframe, a burn on the kitchen counter—yet repeatedly insists that she feels "nothing, nothing at all." In the final line, she writes that she took the doorframe's paint chip home "by accident" in her pocket.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best describes the speaker as presented in the poem?
choices: She is angry at her family for selling the house without her.
She claims to be indifferent to the house, but her actions reveal a strong attachment to it.
She has forgotten most of what happened in the house.
She is relieved that the house is finally being sold.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: U hech narsa his qilmayman desa-da, xonalarni batafsil eslashi va bo'yoq bo'lagini olib ketishi uyga chuqur bog'liqligini ko'rsatadi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: When Mariam Tahiri opened a small bookshop in her neighborhood, friends warned her that online retailers would drive her out of business. Instead of competing on price, Tahiri focused on what websites could not easily offer: weekly reading clubs, author visits, and personal recommendations from staff who knew customers by name. Within three years, the shop had a loyal following, and regular customers said they came as much for the community as for the books.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Tahiri's friends helped her run the bookshop's reading clubs.
Tahiri lowered her prices to compete with online retailers.
Online retailers have stopped selling books in Tahiri's neighborhood.
Tahiri's bookshop succeeded by offering community experiences that online stores could not easily provide.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Do'kon narx bilan emas, balki onlayn do'konlar bera olmaydigan jamoaviy tajribalar orqali muvaffaqiyatga erishgan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Marine biologist Keiko Arai studied how sea otters in a California estuary affect the eelgrass beds where they feed. Otters eat large numbers of crabs, and crabs normally eat the tiny sea slugs that graze algae off eelgrass leaves. When otters returned to the estuary, crab populations fell, sea slugs multiplied, and the slugs kept the eelgrass clean of smothering algae. Arai found that eelgrass beds grew noticeably healthier in areas where otters were most active.
