Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Qo'shiqlarning port tavernalari kitoblarida kema jurnallaridan bir necha yil oldin paydo bo'lgani ular quruqlikda paydo bo'lganini ko'rsatadi. A variant ikkala gipotezaga ham mos.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Archaeologist Rustam Karimov excavated a settlement in the Fergana Valley dating to around 500 BCE. Because the site contained many spindle whorls (weights used in spinning thread), Karimov hypothesizes that textile production was a major activity carried out in most households there rather than a specialized trade concentrated in a few workshops. Such objects are common at ancient sites across Central Asia, and Karimov's team excavated more than forty houses at this settlement.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Karimov's hypothesis?
choices: Spindle whorls at the site were made of both clay and stone.
Nearly all the spindle whorls at the site were found clustered together in two large buildings near the settlement's center.
Pottery at the site was decorated with patterns resembling those found on woven fabric.
Spindle whorls were found in nearly every house excavated at the site, typically in small numbers near the hearth.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Deyarli har bir uyda urchuq toshlarining topilishi to'qimachilik ko'pchilik xonadonlarda bajarilganini ko'rsatadi; ikki binoda to'planishi esa aksincha bo'lardi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Entomologist Matteo Russo hypothesizes that honeybees returning to their hive communicate the distance to a food source mainly through the duration of the "waggle" portion of their dance, rather than through the number of times they repeat the dance. Scientists have known for decades that foraging bees perform dances that convey information about where food can be found. Russo conducted experiments in which he placed sugar-water feeders at various locations around several hives.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Russo's hypothesis?
choices: Bees that danced more times attracted more hive mates to follow them.
Bees from different hives performed dances that looked broadly similar.

When researchers moved a feeder progressively farther from the hive, the waggle portion of returning bees' dances grew longer in step with the distance, while the number of repetitions varied mainly with the sweetness of the food.
Waggle dances were performed more often in summer than in spring.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Masofa oshgani sayin tebranish davomiyligi uzaygani, takrorlar soni esa ozuqa shirinligiga bog'liqligi masofa davomiylik orqali bildirilishini tasdiqlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is adapted from Winifred Aske's 1896 novel The Drover's Road. Hester, who manages her family's sheep farm, is negotiating the sale of her flock with a merchant who assumes she knows little about the trade. Since her father's death, Hester has run the farm on her own, though few people in the district believe a woman can manage it well.

A critic argues that Hester strategically allows the merchant to underestimate her.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from The Drover's Road most effectively illustrates the critic's argument?
choices: "Hester had kept the farm's accounts since her father's death, and she knew the value of every animal in the flock."
"She corrected him at once, reciting the price of wool in every market from York to Carlisle."

"She let him explain the price of wool at length, nodding as though each figure were a revelation, and only when he had committed himself to terms did she mention the letter from the Leeds mill offering a third more."
"The merchant spoke slowly and loudly, as one might to a child, and Hester felt her face grow hot with anger."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: To'g'ri iqtibosda Hester savdogarga o'zini bilmaydigandek ko'rsatadi, so'ng u shartlarga rozi bo'lgach kuchli dalilni chiqaradi; bu strategik harakatni ko'rsatadi. A variant uning bilimini ko'rsatadi, lekin strategiyasini emas.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Nutrition researcher Fatima Belhaj hypothesizes that eating breakfast improves students' concentration during morning classes. To test this, she compared students who regularly ate breakfast with students who regularly skipped it at several secondary schools in Morocco. Although it is widely believed that breakfast helps students learn, relatively few studies have directly measured its effects on attention. Belhaj gave all participating students the same set of concentration tasks during the morning.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Belhaj's hypothesis?
choices: Students who ate breakfast and students who skipped it performed equally well on concentration tasks given at 10 a.m.
Most students who skipped breakfast said they did so because they were not hungry in the morning.
Students who ate breakfast scored higher on concentration tasks given at 10 a.m. than students who skipped it.
Students who ate breakfast were more likely to arrive at school on time.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Agar nonushta qilgan va qilmagan talabalarning diqqati bir xil bo'lsa, nonushta diqqatni yaxshilaydi degan gipoteza zaiflashadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Political scientist Ingrid Solberg hypothesizes that voter turnout in local elections in Norway increased after municipalities began holding those elections on the same day as national elections because the combined schedule reduced the effort needed to vote, not because voters became more interested in local issues. Before the change, turnout in local elections had been considerably lower than turnout in national ones. Solberg analyzed voting records and conducted surveys of voters.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Solberg's hypothesis?
choices: Turnout in the combined elections rose even among voters who reported that voting on the same day saved them no time or travel, and surveys showed a marked rise in interest in local issues during the same period.
Turnout in local elections rose by about ten percentage points after the change.
Municipalities that kept separate election days saw no change in local turnout.
Most voters said they found it convenient to vote in both elections at once.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Vaqt tejalmagan saylovchilarda ham qatnashish oshgani va mahalliy masalalarga qiziqish ko'tarilgani o'sish qulaylik tufayli emas, qiziqish tufayli ekanini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Sociolinguist Oydin Rahimova studies Tashkent residents who speak both Uzbek and Russian. She hypothesizes that speakers switch from Uzbek to Russian mid-conversation primarily to signal a shift to a more formal or technical topic, rather than because they cannot recall the relevant Uzbek words. Both languages are widely used in the city, and many residents move between them freely in everyday speech. Rahimova recorded conversations among bilingual speakers in homes and workplaces.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Rahimova's hypothesis?
choices: Younger speakers switched between languages less often than older speakers.
When asked to translate technical Russian terms into Uzbek, many speakers were unable to do so.

Speakers who switched to Russian when discussing topics such as engineering or law readily supplied the equivalent Uzbek terms when asked afterward, and they seldom switched when discussing family matters.
Speakers switched to Russian more often when they were tired or distracted.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: So'zlovchilar o'zbekcha atamalarni bilgani holda rasmiy mavzularda ruschaga o'tishi o'tish so'z unutish emas, mavzuni belgilash uchun ekanini ko'rsatadi. B variant gipotezani zaiflashtiradi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is from Clementine Ashby's 1912 novel The Winter Loom. Agnes, a weaver, has entered one of her tapestries in a regional competition. Agnes has spent the entire autumn working on the piece, often late into the night after her other chores were done.

A reviewer claims that Agnes is outwardly modest about her work but privately proud of it.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from The Winter Loom most effectively illustrates the reviewer's claim?
choices: "Agnes had learned to weave from her grandmother, who had used the same loom for fifty years."
"'It is only a small thing,' she told the judges, lowering her eyes; but that night she lit a second candle just to look at it longer, smiling at the border she had labored over all autumn."
"She had chosen deep blues and greens for the design because those threads were the cheapest at the market."
"The competition hall was crowded with tapestries from every village in the county."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: To'g'ri iqtibosda Agnes hakamlarga kamtarona gapiradi, lekin yolg'iz qolganda asaridan faxrlanadi; bu ikkala qismni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is from Beatrix Moreland's 1906 novel Ashes on the Hearth. Julian, a once-famous painter, has not exhibited his work in over a decade. Critics once hailed him as the most promising artist of his generation, and his sudden silence remains a subject of gossip.

A student claims that Julian continues to paint in secret even though he tells others he has given up art.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from Ashes on the Hearth most effectively illustrates the student's claim?
choices: "Julian spent his afternoons walking along the river, pausing now and then to watch the light change on the water."
"The paintings that had made his name still hung in the city gallery, their colors slowly fading."
"'I have not touched a brush in ten years,' he told the young critic, and he seemed almost proud of it."
"'I have not touched a brush in ten years,' he told the young critic; yet when the maid swept his study the next morning, she found fresh blue paint drying on the edge of the washbasin."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: To'g'ri iqtibosda Julian rasm chizmaganini aytadi, lekin xizmatchi yangi bo'yoq izlarini topadi; bu yashirincha chizishni ko'rsatadi. C variantda faqat da'vo bor, dalil yo'q.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Astronomer Ekaterina Volkova studies a star whose brightness dips briefly every 47 days. Volkova hypothesizes that the dips are caused by a planet passing in front of the star rather than by dark spots rotating across the star's surface. Periodic dips in a star's brightness can have more than one cause. A planet passing between the star and Earth blocks some of its light, but large dark spots on a rotating star can produce similar dips. Volkova has been monitoring the star for several years.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Volkova's hypothesis?
choices: Several other stars of similar size are known to have planets that orbit them.
The star is somewhat cooler and smaller than the Sun.
Measurements show that the star rotates once every 47 days and that the depth and shape of each dip change gradually from one cycle to the next, as spots typically do when they grow and fade.
The dips last about the same length of time in every cycle.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Yulduz aynan 47 kunda aylanishi va pasayishlar shakli asta o'zgarishi dog'larga xos; bu sayyora gipotezasini zaiflashtiradi. D variant aksincha sayyoraga mos keladi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Ecologist Samuel Achterberg hypothesizes that the recent decline of a certain butterfly species in the Netherlands is caused mainly by the loss of the single plant species its caterpillars feed on, rather than by rising temperatures. The butterfly's caterpillars can eat only one plant, a wildflower whose meadow habitat has been shrinking as farmland expands. At the same time, average temperatures in the region have been climbing. Achterberg compared butterfly counts across many regions.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Achterberg's hypothesis?
choices: Adult butterflies of the species feed on nectar from many kinds of flowers.
Temperatures in the Netherlands have risen steadily over the past thirty years.
Other butterfly species in the Netherlands have also declined in number.
In regions where the caterpillars' food plant remained abundant, butterfly populations stayed stable even though temperatures there rose as much as elsewhere.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Harorat bir xil ko'tarilgan bo'lsa ham, ozuqa o'simligi saqlangan joylarda kapalaklar soni barqaror qolishi asosiy sabab o'simlik yo'qolishi ekanini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Red rock layers are found in many parts of the world, and geologists have proposed different explanations for their coloring. Geologist Tendai Moyo hypothesizes that the unusual red color of rock layers in a Zimbabwean canyon formed because iron in the sediments was exposed to oxygen-rich air while the sediments lay on dry land, rather than because the sediments were deposited underwater.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Moyo's hypothesis?
choices: The red layers are rich in iron compared with the rock layers above them.
The red layers are located directly above gray layers that contain fossil fish.
The canyon was carved by a river that still flows through it today.
The red layers contain fossilized raindrop impressions, mud cracks, and footprints of land animals, but no fossils of aquatic organisms.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Yomg'ir tomchisi izlari, loy yoriqlari va quruqlik hayvonlari izlari cho'kindilar quruqlikda bo'lganini ko'rsatadi. Temir miqdori (A variant) quruqlikda yoki suvda ekanini ajratmaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Economic historian Ayodele Bankole studies the West African cowrie-shell currency system of the eighteenth century. Cowrie shells, small seashells from the Indian Ocean, served as money in many West African markets for centuries. She hypothesizes that the massive import of cowrie shells by European traders led to inflation in local prices, since more shells were chasing the same quantity of goods.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Bankole's hypothesis?
choices: European traders imported cowrie shells from the Maldives, far across the Indian Ocean.
The price of imported cloth, measured in shells, fluctuated from year to year.

Market records from several trading towns show that the number of shells needed to buy a fixed quantity of staple goods such as yams and salt rose steadily during the decades when shell imports were highest, while harvests remained stable.
Cowrie shells were also used as decorations and in religious ceremonies.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Import eng yuqori bo'lgan davrda hosil barqaror qolgani holda asosiy mahsulotlar narxi (chig'anoqlarda) oshgani inflyatsiyani ko'rsatadi. B variant faqat tebranishni ko'rsatadi, izchil o'sishni emas.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Sociologist Amara Nwosu hypothesizes that public libraries that extend their evening hours see increased use mainly by working adults, who are unable to visit during the day. Several public libraries in Nigeria have recently extended their closing times from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m. on weekdays. Library directors have reported that overall visits increased after the change, but it is not yet clear which groups account for the increase. Nwosu surveyed visitors at these libraries.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Nwosu's hypothesis?
choices: Evening hours cost libraries more in staffing than morning hours did.
After libraries added evening hours, most of the new evening visitors reported having full-time daytime jobs.
After libraries added evening hours, overall daytime attendance stayed roughly the same.
Libraries that added evening hours also expanded their children's book collections.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Yangi kechki tashrifchilarning ko'pchiligi kunduzi ishlaydigan kattalar bo'lsa, bu gipotezani bevosita tasdiqlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Behavioral economist Hyun-woo Park hypothesizes that students are more likely to choose a healthy snack at a school cafeteria when it is placed at eye level, not because they notice it more, but because they interpret its prominent placement as a recommendation from the school. Several schools in Seoul have experimented with rearranging cafeteria displays to encourage healthier eating. Park conducted a series of experiments in which the position of snacks and the information given to students were varied.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Park's hypothesis?
choices: Students chose healthy snacks more often when the snacks were placed at eye level.
Eye-tracking showed that students looked at eye-level snacks more often than at snacks on lower shelves.
Healthy snacks at the cafeteria cost slightly more than less healthy ones.

When a sign explained that snack placement had been chosen randomly, placing healthy snacks at eye level no longer increased how often students chose them, even though students still noticed them just as often.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Joylashuv tasodifiy ekani aytilganda, e'tibor bir xil bo'lsa ham ta'sir yo'qolgani ta'sir 'tavsiya' deb talqin qilishdan kelishini ko'rsatadi. B variant raqib tushuntirishni (e'tibor) qo'llaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is from Horatio Blackwood's 1887 poem "The Ferryman's Evening." The speaker is an old ferryman reflecting on his life. The poem is written as a monologue spoken at the end of a working day. He has operated the same ferry for most of his life.

A scholar claims that the speaker views his repetitive work not as a burden but as a source of quiet meaning.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from "The Ferryman's Evening" most effectively illustrates the scholar's claim?
choices: "The river rises in the spring and sinks in autumn's drought; / the reeds along the bank grow tall, then brown, then die."
"My father rowed this water, and his father rowed before; / they sleep now in the churchyard where the ferry cannot go."
"Ten thousand crossings, and my arms have grown as stiff as oars; / I dream of roads that go somewhere and do not come back."
"Ten thousand crossings, and the river never twice the same; / each face I carried over left its small light in the boat."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: To'g'ri iqtibosda takroriy ish (o'n ming o'tish) mazmunli sifatida tasvirlangan: har bir yo'lovchi 'kichik nur' qoldirgan. C variant ishni yuk sifatida ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is adapted from Edmund Harrow's 1888 play The Miller's Wager. Thomas, a miller, has bet his neighbor that his old mill can grind more grain in a day than the neighbor's new steam-powered one. The neighbor's mill has already drawn away several of Thomas's longtime customers.

A critic argues that Thomas's confidence masks a deep fear that his way of life is becoming obsolete.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from The Miller's Wager most effectively illustrates the critic's argument?
choices: "THOMAS: My father built this wheel with his own hands, and a fine wheel it is."
"THOMAS: Martha, fetch the good flour sacks—the ones with the red stitching."
"THOMAS (laughing loudly, then turning away): Let them bring their steam and smoke! (quietly, to himself) And if the wheel fails me, what am I then but an old man beside a stream?"
"THOMAS: The river has run past this mill for a hundred years, and it has never once asked for coal."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: To'g'ri iqtibosda Tomas baland ovozda kuladi, lekin o'ziga-o'zi eskirib qolishdan qo'rqishini aytadi; bu ishonch ortidagi qo'rquvni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is adapted from Rowena Thistlewood's 1910 novel The Keeper of Bees. Old Mrs. Pell has lived alone on the moor for many years. The village children are both frightened of her and fascinated by the hives that crowd her garden. Few of them have ever seen her smile.

A critic claims that Mrs. Pell, despite her gruff manner, cares deeply for the village children.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from The Keeper of Bees most effectively illustrates the critic's claim?
choices: "She scolded the children off her gate with a stick and a sharp tongue, and they learned to give her cottage a wide berth."
"Mrs. Pell had outlived her husband, her brothers, and most of her friends."
"She scolded the children off her gate with a stick and a sharp tongue, yet every autumn a basket of honeycomb appeared, unsigned, on the schoolhouse step."
"Her bees were said to produce the finest heather honey in the county."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: To'g'ri iqtibos qo'pol tashqi ko'rinish (bolalarni haydash) va yashirin g'amxo'rlik (asal savati) ni birga ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Ecologist Nomvula Dlamini studies dung beetles in South African grasslands. She hypothesizes that dung beetles roll their dung balls in straight lines away from the dung pile by orienting themselves to the Milky Way on moonless nights, not only by using the moon or nearby landmarks. Dung beetles move their balls away from the pile quickly to avoid competitors who might steal them. Dlamini conducted experiments both in the field and inside a planetarium.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Dlamini's hypothesis?
choices: On moonless nights in an open planetarium arena with no landmarks, beetles rolled in straight lines when only the Milky Way was projected overhead but wandered in circles when the dome was completely dark.
Beetles rolled their balls in straight lines on nights when the moon was full.
Beetles rolled in less straight lines on cloudy nights than on clear nights.
Beetles that were fitted with small caps blocking their view of the sky took longer to roll their balls away from the pile.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Belgi va oy bo'lmagan sharoitda faqat Somon yo'li ko'rsatilganda qo'ng'izlar to'g'ri harakatlangani ular aynan Somon yo'liga tayanishini ko'rsatadi. C va D variantlar osmonni muhimligini ko'rsatadi, lekin Somon yo'lini oy yoki yulduzlardan ajratmaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Physiologist Oskar Lindqvist hypothesizes that reindeer in northern Scandinavia can see ultraviolet light and that this ability helps them spot lichen, a key winter food, against snow. Snow reflects most ultraviolet light, whereas lichen absorbs it. Humans cannot see ultraviolet light, but a number of animals, including many insects and birds, can. Lindqvist tested reindeer in controlled outdoor enclosures during the winter months, when lichen is often the only food available to them.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Lindqvist's hypothesis?
choices: Lichen grows more slowly in northern Scandinavia than in more southern regions.
Reindeer located patches of lichen on snow more quickly under natural light than under light from which ultraviolet wavelengths had been filtered out.
Reindeer spend more time grazing in winter than in summer.
Many Arctic birds are also able to see ultraviolet light.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Ultrabinafsha nur olib tashlanganda bug'ular likenni sekinroq topishi ular aynan UB nurdan foydalanishini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Climatologist Farida Nazarova hypothesizes that the shrinking of glaciers in the Pamir Mountains over the past forty years has been driven more by a decrease in winter snowfall than by an increase in summer temperatures. Glaciers in the Pamirs supply water to millions of people downstream, so understanding why they are shrinking has practical importance. Nazarova analyzed decades of weather-station data from the region.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Nazarova's hypothesis?
choices: Winter snowfall in the Pamirs has declined steadily over the past forty years.
Meltwater from Pamir glaciers is an important source of water for farms downstream.
Winter snowfall in the Pamirs has remained essentially constant over the past forty years, while average summer temperatures have risen by more than one degree Celsius.
Glaciers in neighboring mountain ranges have also shrunk over the same period.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Qor miqdori o'zgarmagan, yozgi harorat esa oshgan bo'lsa, muzliklarning qisqarishini qor kamayishi bilan izohlab bo'lmaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Education researcher Lars Magnusson studied a program in Swedish schools that reduced class sizes from twenty-eight to eighteen students. Test scores rose in participating schools. Magnusson hypothesizes that the improvement resulted from teachers giving more individual feedback to each student in smaller classes, rather than from a reduction in classroom disruptions. The program was introduced in a group of schools while other similar schools kept their original class sizes.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Magnusson's hypothesis?
choices: Classroom observations showed that teachers in smaller classes gave individual students about the same amount of feedback as before, while the number of disruptions per lesson fell by more than half.
Test scores rose most in schools where teachers spent the most time giving individual feedback.
Teachers in smaller classes reported feeling less stressed at the end of the school day.
Students in smaller classes said they felt more comfortable asking questions.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Individual fikr-mulohaza o'zgarmagan, lekin tartibsizliklar keskin kamaygan bo'lsa, yaxshilanish raqib sabab — tartibsizlik kamayishi — bilan izohlanadi; bu gipotezani zaiflashtiradi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Historian Beatriz Almeida studies letters written by Portuguese merchants in the 1600s. She hypothesizes that the merchants frequently exaggerated the dangers of sea voyages in their letters in order to justify charging higher prices to customers back home. The letters, which were sent to relatives, business partners, and customers, describe storms, shipwrecks, and pirate attacks in vivid detail. Almeida compared them with other records from the same period.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Almeida's hypothesis?
choices: The merchants' letters frequently mentioned the names of the ships on which goods were carried.

Ships' logs from the same voyages recorded far fewer storms and pirate attacks than the merchants described in their letters, and the letters containing the most dramatic accounts were sent to buyers rather than to family members.
Many of the merchants had learned to write at church schools in Lisbon.
Sea voyages in the 1600s often took several months to complete.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Kema jurnallari kamroq xavfni qayd etgani va eng dramatik xatlar xaridorlarga yuborilgani savdogarlar narxni oqlash uchun mubolag'a qilganini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Primatologist Esther Mwangi hypothesizes that young chimpanzees in a Ugandan forest learn to crack nuts with stones primarily by watching their mothers rather than through their own trial and error. Nut cracking is a difficult skill that takes young chimpanzees several years to master, and researchers have debated how the skill is passed on. Mwangi observed several mother-offspring pairs over many years.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Mwangi's hypothesis?
choices: Adult chimpanzees in the forest cracked nuts mainly during the dry season.

Young chimpanzees whose mothers cracked nuts frequently mastered the skill much earlier than young chimpanzees whose mothers rarely did, and they closely copied their mothers' particular grip and striking angle.
Young chimpanzees made many unsuccessful attempts to crack nuts before they succeeded.
Chimpanzees in the forest used several types of stones as hammers.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Onalari tez-tez yong'oq chaqqan bolalar ertaroq o'rganib, onalarining usulini aynan takrorlagani kuzatish orqali o'rganishni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is adapted from Esmé Laurent's 1914 novel The Glasshouse. Imogen, a botanist's widow, has decided to continue her late husband's research on orchids. Her husband was a respected scientist, and Imogen spent decades as his household manager and hostess, rarely mentioned in his published papers.

A critic argues that Imogen's dedication to the research is motivated less by grief than by her own long-suppressed scientific ambition.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from The Glasshouse most effectively illustrates the critic's argument?
choices: "Friends urged her to sell the collection and return to the city, but she would not hear of it."
"The orchids required constant attention, and Imogen rose at dawn each day to adjust the glasshouse vents."

"Reading his notes, she found herself correcting his figures in the margin, as she had longed to do for twenty years while she sat silent at his dinner table; the work, she realized, had always been half hers."
"She kept his pen and spectacles on the desk exactly as he had left them, and she could not bring herself to move them."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: To'g'ri iqtibos Imogenning yillar davomida bostirilgan ilmiy intilishini ochiq ko'rsatadi. D variant qayg'uni, A variant esa sababsiz qat'iyatni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is from Philippa Grey's 1891 novel The Tidewater House. Rosalind, a young widow, has inherited a large but crumbling estate. Her late husband's relatives have urged her to sell it, and the local lawyer has quietly told her that the house is beyond saving.

The narrator suggests that Rosalind is determined to restore the estate despite others' doubts.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from The Tidewater House most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: "The house stood on a low hill overlooking the marsh, its windows clouded with salt."
"When the lawyer advised her to sell before the roof gave way entirely, Rosalind merely rolled up her sleeves and asked where she might find a reliable carpenter."
"Rosalind's late husband had rarely visited the estate, preferring the society of the town."
"In the evenings she read old letters she had found in a trunk in the attic."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Advokat sotishni maslahat berganda ham Rosalindning duradgor izlashi uning qat'iyatini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage:
The following text is adapted from Obadiah Fenwick's 1893 story "The Clockmaker's Apprentice." Peter, an apprentice, is repairing an antique clock for a wealthy client while his master is away. It is the first time Peter has been trusted with such a valuable piece, and the client is known throughout the town for being hard to please.

A student claims that Peter lacks confidence in his own abilities.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which quotation from "The Clockmaker's Apprentice" most effectively illustrates the student's claim?
choices: "The clock had been built in Geneva nearly a century earlier and had passed through many owners."
"The client had left strict instructions that the clock be ready by Friday."

"Each time the tiny gears slipped into place, Peter pulled them out again, certain that his master would have done it better, until the lamp burned low and the clock lay in more pieces than when he began."
"Peter set to work with steady hands, humming a tune his master had taught him."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Petrning to'g'ri o'rnatilgan tishli g'ildiraklarni 'ustoz yaxshiroq qilardi' deb qayta olib tashlashi o'ziga ishonchsizlikni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Physician-researcher Hamid Karimi studies a medication that lowers blood pressure. Patients taking it also report fewer headaches. Karimi hypothesizes that the medication reduces headaches through a separate action on blood vessels in the brain, not merely as a side effect of lowering overall blood pressure. Karimi reviewed data from clinical trials of the medication and compared it with trials of other blood pressure drugs.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Karimi's hypothesis?
choices: Patients with the highest blood pressure before treatment reported the greatest reduction in headaches.

Patients whose blood pressure was lowered by the same amount using a different medication reported no reduction in headaches, whereas patients taking Karimi's medication reported fewer headaches even when their blood pressure barely changed.
Headaches are a common complaint among patients with high blood pressure.
Patients taking the medication experienced larger drops in blood pressure than patients taking a placebo.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Bosimni boshqa dori bilan xuddi shunday tushirish bosh og'rig'ini kamaytirmagani va bu dori bosimni o'zgartirmasa ham og'riqni kamaytirgani alohida ta'sirni ko'rsatadi. A variant raqib tushuntirishga mos keladi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Agricultural scientist Chen Yuling hypothesizes that planting rows of sunflowers alongside rice paddies reduces damage from insect pests because the sunflowers attract predatory wasps that feed on the pests. Insect pests cause serious losses in rice crops across southern China, and many farmers hope to reduce their reliance on chemical pesticides. Chen compared pest damage in paddies with and without sunflower borders across two growing seasons, and also counted the predatory wasps present in each paddy.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Chen's hypothesis?
choices: Predatory wasps are known to feed on several different species of rice pests.
Paddies bordered by sunflowers had no more predatory wasps than paddies without sunflowers, yet both groups showed similar levels of pest damage.
Paddies bordered by sunflowers had more predatory wasps and less pest damage than paddies without sunflowers.
Sunflowers planted near rice paddies produced a large harvest of seeds that farmers could sell.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Kungaboqar arilar sonini oshirmagan va zarar kamaymagan bo'lsa, gipotezadagi mexanizm ham, natija ham tasdiqlanmaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Ornithologist Kwame Asante hypothesizes that great tits living in noisy city parks sing at higher pitches than rural great tits because higher-pitched songs are easier to hear over low-frequency traffic noise, not because city birds are genetically different. Researchers have observed this difference in pitch in cities around the world. Asante recorded songs from birds in parks in Accra and in nearby rural areas over several months.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Asante's hypothesis?
choices: Rural great tits sang more frequently in the early morning than urban great tits did.
Urban and rural great tits showed small but consistent genetic differences.
Urban great tits were found to be slightly smaller on average than rural great tits.
When traffic noise was temporarily reduced during a citywide road closure, urban birds lowered the pitch of their songs within days, then raised it again when traffic returned.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Shovqin kamayganda qushlar bir necha kunda ohangni pasaytirib, keyin qayta ko'tarishi bu genetik farq emas, shovqinga moslashuv ekanini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Archaeologist Malia Kahananui studies stone fishponds built along the coasts of Hawai'i. Some of these ponds cover many hectares and are enclosed by stone walls hundreds of meters long. Some scholars believe the ponds were constructed gradually by individual families over many generations. Kahananui hypothesizes instead that most large ponds were built in single, coordinated construction campaigns directed by regional chiefs.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Kahananui's hypothesis?
choices: The largest ponds covered several hectares and required enormous quantities of stone.
Oral histories describe families harvesting fish from the ponds for many generations.
Radiocarbon dates from materials sealed within the walls of the largest ponds cluster tightly within a few decades, and the walls show a uniform building technique along their entire length.
Smaller ponds were found at more locations along the coast than larger ponds were.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Devorlardagi radiokarbon sanalarning bir necha o'n yillikda to'planishi va bir xil qurilish uslubi yagona muvofiqlashtirilgan qurilishni ko'rsatadi. To'g'ri variantdan tashqari hech biri qurilish vaqtini ko'rsatmaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
An urban ecologist planted four garden plots with different numbers of flowering plant species and counted how often bees visited each plot.

  Plot — Flower species planted — Bee visits per hour
  Plot 1 — 3 — 22
  Plot 2 — 6 — 41
  Plot 3 — 9 — 63
  Plot 4 — 12 — 80

Pollinators such as bees are declining in many cities, so ecologists are looking for simple ways to support them. After a summer of observations, the ecologist concluded that plots with a greater variety of flowers attracted more bees. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Plot 2 had 6 flower species and received 63 bee visits per hour.
Plot 3 received more bee visits per hour than Plot 4 did.
Plot 4, which had 12 flower species, received 80 bee visits per hour, while Plot 1, which had only 3 species, received 22.
Each plot was planted with a different number of flower species.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Jadvalga ko'ra, 12 tur ekilgan 4-uchastkaga soatiga 80 marta, 3 tur ekilgan 1-uchastkaga esa atigi 22 marta asalari kelgan; bu turlar ko'payishi bilan tashriflar ortganini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
The graph shows the number of e-book loans and print-book loans at Riverside Public Library in three years.

  2019: e-books 12,000; print books 88,000
  2021: e-books 31,000; print books 70,000

choices: E-book loans exceeded print loans in 2023.
Print loans rose each year from 2019 to 2023.
E-book loans rose from 12,000 in 2019 to 47,000 in 2023, but print loans (61,000) still exceeded e-book loans in 2023.
Total loans in 2021 were 101,000.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo ikki qismdan iborat: elektron kitoblar ulushi o'smoqda va bosma kitoblar hali ham ko'p. 2023-yilda e-kitoblar 47 000 ga yetgan, ammo bosma kitoblar (61 000) hamon ko'proq.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
A city planner compared tree canopy cover with summer temperatures in four neighborhoods.

  Elm Park — 42% — 29.1°C

  Midtown — 8% — 33.8°C

choices: Dockside had more canopy cover than Hillcrest did.
Midtown had the lowest average July afternoon temperature of the four neighborhoods.
Hillcrest had 30% canopy cover.
Elm Park, with 42% canopy cover, had an average July afternoon temperature of 29.1°C, nearly 5 degrees cooler than Midtown, with 8% cover.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Eng ko'p daraxt soyasi bo'lgan Elm Park (42%) eng kam soyali Midtowndan (8%) deyarli 5 daraja salqinroq bo'lgan, bu daraxtlar sovitishini qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Researchers studying users of a language-learning app compared daily practice time with vocabulary retention.

  Minutes practiced per day — Average words retained after 8 weeks
  5 — 140
  10 — 260
  20 — 410
  30 — 450

The researchers found that learners who practiced longer generally retained more words. However, they noted that the benefit of additional practice time appeared to shrink at higher levels of practice: ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: learners who practiced 30 minutes a day retained an average of 450 words.
learners who practiced 5 minutes a day retained more words than those who practiced 10 minutes a day.
increasing practice from 10 to 20 minutes raised retention by 150 words, but increasing it from 20 to 30 minutes raised retention by only 40 words.
increasing practice from 20 to 30 minutes raised retention by 150 words.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: 10 dan 20 daqiqaga o'tish 150 so'z (410−260), 20 dan 30 ga o'tish esa atigi 40 so'z (450−410) qo'shgan; bu qo'shimcha foyda kamayib borishini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
A sustainability officer compared recycling in four apartment buildings with different recycling-bin locations.

  Building — Bin location — Share of waste recycled

  B — every floor — 51%
  C — basement only — 22%
  D — basement only — 19%

choices: Building C recycled a larger share of its waste than Building A did.
Building D had bins on every floor and recycled 19% of its waste.
Building B recycled 51% of its waste.
Buildings A and B, which had bins on every floor, recycled 46% and 51% of their waste, while Buildings C and D, with basement-only bins, recycled 22% and 19%.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Har qavatda qutisi bo'lgan binolar (46% va 51%) faqat yerto'lada qutisi bo'lgan binolardan (22% va 19%) ancha ko'p qayta ishlagan; bu gipotezani tasdiqlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
The graph shows the average daily electricity output of a rooftop solar-panel system in each season of one year.

  Winter: 9.8 kWh
  Spring: 18.6 kWh
  Summer: 24.1 kWh
  Autumn: 14.2 kWh

Solar output depends on both the length of the day and the angle of the sun. After tracking her system for a full year, a homeowner claims that it produced more than twice as much electricity per day in summer as it did in winter.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the homeowner's claim?
choices: Average daily output was 18.6 kWh in spring and 14.2 kWh in autumn.
Average daily output was 24.1 kWh in summer and 9.8 kWh in winter.
Average daily output was 24.1 kWh in summer and 14.2 kWh in winter.
Average daily output was higher in autumn than in spring.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Yozda 24.1 kVt·soat, qishda 9.8 kVt·soat; 9.8 ning ikki barobari 19.6 ga teng, 24.1 undan katta, demak da'vo to'g'ri.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
A school district tracked late arrivals at three schools before and after it began serving free breakfast before the first bell.

  School — Tardy arrivals per week (before) — (after)
  Northside — 64 — 31
  Lakeview — 48 — 22
  Central — 71 — 40

District officials had hoped that offering breakfast would encourage students to arrive on time. At the end of the year, the district reported that tardiness decreased at every school in the program. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: At each of the three schools, weekly tardy arrivals fell after the program began; at Lakeview, for example, they dropped from 48 to 22.
At Central, weekly tardy arrivals rose from 40 to 71 after the program began.
Northside had the most tardy arrivals per week before the program began.
Lakeview had fewer tardy arrivals per week than Northside did before the program began.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Uchala maktabda ham kechikishlar kamaygan (masalan, Lakeviewda 48 dan 22 ga), bu 'har bir maktabda' degan da'voni qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Marine biologists recorded the peak water temperature and the extent of coral bleaching at a reef in four years.

  Year — Peak water temperature — Share of reef bleached
  2014 — 29.2°C — 12%

  2018 — 29.6°C — 18%

choices: The share of the reef that was bleached increased in every year listed.
In 2018, the peak water temperature was 30.8°C.
The reef was monitored in four different years.
In 2020, when peak water temperature reached 31.1°C, 55% of the reef was bleached, compared with 12% in 2014, when the peak was 29.2°C.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Eng issiq yil 2020 (31.1°C) da riflarning 55% i, eng salqin yil 2014 (29.2°C) da esa atigi 12% i oqargan; bu harorat va oqarish bog'liqligini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
The graph shows the average number of daily visitors to a history museum on different types of days.

  Paid-admission weekends: 540

choices: Average attendance was 820 on free weekdays versus 310 on paid weekdays, and 1,150 on free weekends versus 540 on paid weekends.
Average attendance was higher on paid weekends (540) than on paid weekdays (310).
Average attendance on free weekdays was lower than on paid weekends.
Average attendance was 1,150 on free weekends and 820 on free weekdays.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Xulosa bepul va pullik kunlarni ham ish kunlarida, ham dam olish kunlarida solishtirishni talab qiladi; faqat to'g'ri javob ikkala juftlikni ham taqqoslaydi.

A student grew basil plants under four colors of LED light and measured their heights after 30 days.

  Light color — Average height after 30 days

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Basil grown under white light was taller than basil grown under red and blue light together.
Basil grown under red and blue light together reached an average of 24 cm, taller than basil grown under red (18 cm), blue (14 cm), or white (19 cm) light.
Basil grown under blue light reached an average height of 18 cm.
Basil grown under red light was taller than basil grown under blue light.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Qizil va ko'k yorug'lik ostida rayhon 24 sm ga yetgan, bu qolgan barcha sharoitlardan (18, 14, 19 sm) baland; aynan shu da'voni isbotlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Psychologists compared the test scores of students who took lecture notes by hand with those of students who typed notes on laptops.

  Note-taking method — Average score, factual questions — Average score, conceptual questions
  Handwritten — 81 — 78
  Typed on laptop — 80 — 64

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Typed note-takers scored higher on conceptual questions than on factual questions.
Handwritten note-takers scored an average of 78 on factual questions.
Handwritten and typed note-takers scored almost the same on factual questions (81 and 80), but handwritten note-takers scored 14 points higher on conceptual questions (78 versus 64).
Handwritten note-takers scored higher on factual questions than on conceptual questions.

choices: In 2022, the fleet included 45 electric buses and 160 diesel buses.

  Professional outdoor photo — 19

dogs with no photo were adopted faster than dogs photographed in kennels.
dogs with professional outdoor photos waited an average of 33 days for adoption.
the shelter posted three types of listings on its website.

Of the 200 saplings planted without mulch, 172 survived.
The volunteers planted a total of 400 saplings.

More than half of adults aged 30–44 listened to a podcast in the past month.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Birdwatchers in a suburban park set up four types of feeders and recorded how many bird species visited each one.

  Seed tube — 6

  Nectar — 2

choices: The seed tube feeder drew an average of 11 species per day.
The suet cake feeder drew more species per day than the seed tube feeder did.
The platform feeder with mixed food drew an average of 11 species per day, more than any other feeder.
The nectar feeder drew an average of 2 species per day.

Transportation officials lowered the speed limit on two roads while leaving a third road unchanged, then compared crash numbers.

  Road — Speed limit — Crashes per year (before) — (after)
  Route 1 — lowered from 60 to 40 km/h — 38 — 21
  Route 2 — lowered from 60 to 40 km/h — 29 — 17
  Route 3 — unchanged — 33 — 34

A water utility installed low-flow showerheads in a group of homes at the start of March and tracked household water use.

  Month — Average daily water use per household
  January (before) — 420 liters
  February (before) — 415 liters
  March (after) — 342 liters
  April (after) — 338 liters

Showers account for a large share of indoor water use. Based on these results, a utility manager claimed that installing low-flow showerheads reduced household water use by more than 70 liters per day. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Average daily use was 342 liters in March and 338 liters in April.
Average daily use increased after the showerheads were installed.
Average daily use was 420 liters in January and 415 liters in April.
Average daily use was 415 to 420 liters in the two months before installation and 338 to 342 liters in the two months after.

A school nurse recorded student absences due to illness over three months as the school introduced new hygiene measures.

  Month — Measures in place — Illness-related absences
  October — none — 212

choices: Illness-related absences were higher in December than in November.
Illness-related absences fell by 104 between October and December.

Handwashing posters were displayed in both November and December.

  2018: 14%

  2024: 36%

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the owner's claim?
choices: Online sales made up 14% of total sales in 2018 but 39%, 33%, and 36% in 2020, 2022, and 2024, respectively.
The online share of sales increased in every period shown.
Online sales made up 39% of total sales in 2024.
The online share of sales was lower in 2022 than in 2020.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
A chess coach recorded how many hours four club members practiced each week and how much their tournament ratings changed over one season.

  Player — Weekly practice hours — Rating gain
  Aziza — 2 — +15
  Bekzod — 5 — +48
  Dilnoza — 8 — +90
  Jasur — 11 — +126

The coach often reminds students that steady practice matters more than talent. At the end of the season, the coach claimed that players who practiced more gained more rating points. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?

Bekzod gained 90 rating points over the season.
The coach kept records for four players.
Jasur, who practiced 11 hours a week, gained 126 points, while Aziza, who practiced 2 hours, gained only 15, and gains rose steadily for the players in between.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Mashg'ulot soatlari oshgani sari reyting o'sishi ham oshgan (15, 48, 90, 126); eng ko'p mashq qilgan Jasur eng ko'p ball olgan.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
The owner of an ice cream shop recorded the daily high temperature and the number of cones sold over four days.

  Day — High temperature — Cones sold
  Monday — 24°C — 180
