  Stretching, 3 times a week — +0.6
  No program — −1.8

Simply taking part in a regular group activity might improve memory by providing social contact and routine. For this reason, the stretching group was included for comparison, and the researchers concluded that aerobic exercise specifically, not just regular participation, benefited memory. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: The walking group's scores rose by 4.2 points, far more than the 0.6-point gain in the stretching group, which also met three times a week.
The walking group's scores rose by 4.2 points, while the no-program group's scores fell by 1.8 points.
The stretching group's scores fell by 1.8 points over the twelve months.
The stretching group's scores rose more than the walking group's scores did.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: 'Faqat qatnashish emas' degan xulosani isbotlash uchun yurish guruhini xuddi shunday tez-tez uchrashgan cho'zilish guruhi bilan solishtirish kerak: +4.2 va +0.6.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
The graph shows the share of rural households in a region that used mobile payments and the share that held any formal savings account.

  2016: mobile payments 11%; formal savings 20%
  2019: mobile payments 38%; formal savings 29%
  2022: mobile payments 64%; formal savings 41%
  2025: mobile payments 79%; formal savings 47%

Mobile payment services were expected to draw rural households into the formal financial system. A development economist notes, however, that mobile payment use grew much faster than formal savings did, suggesting that adopting payment technology does not automatically lead to saving at the same pace.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the economist's claim?
choices: Both mobile payment use and formal savings increased in every period shown.
In 2016, more households had formal savings than used mobile payments.
From 2016 to 2025, the share of households using mobile payments rose by 68 percentage points, while the share with formal savings rose by 27 points.
From 2016 to 2025, the share of households with formal savings rose by 68 percentage points.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Mobil to'lovlar ulushi 68 punktga (11% → 79%), jamg'armalar esa atigi 27 punktga (20% → 47%) oshgan; bu o'sish sur'atlaridagi farqni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Civil engineers tested concrete in which different percentages of the usual gravel were replaced with crushed recycled concrete.

  Recycled aggregate — Compressive strength (MPa) — CO2 emissions (kg per m³)
  0% — 42 — 310
  25% — 41 — 285
  50% — 37 — 262
  75% — 30 — 240

Reusing demolition waste could cut both landfill use and emissions. The engineers propose 25% replacement as a promising compromise, because it lowers emissions while leaving strength almost unchanged, unlike higher replacement rates, which weaken the concrete considerably. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: At 75% replacement, emissions fell to 240 kg per m³, the lowest of any mix.
At 25% replacement, strength fell only from 42 to 41 MPa while emissions dropped by 25 kg per m³, whereas at 75% replacement, strength fell to 30 MPa.
At 50% replacement, strength remained at 42 MPa while emissions dropped to 262 kg per m³.
Emissions decreased steadily as the share of recycled aggregate increased.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: 25% da mustahkamlik deyarli o'zgarmagan (42 → 41), emissiya esa 25 kg ga kamaygan; 75% da mustahkamlik 30 MPa gacha tushgan — bu murosani asoslaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
A sociologist analyzed a national survey on volunteering.

  Age group — Share who volunteered in past year — Average hours per volunteer
  18–29 — 31% — 42
  30–49 — 27% — 58
  50–64 — 24% — 81
  65 and older — 22% — 120

Volunteer organizations often focus their recruiting on young people. The sociologist claims that this focus may overlook an important resource: although older adults were somewhat less likely than younger adults to volunteer, older adults who did volunteer contributed far more time. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Average hours per volunteer rose with each older age group.
Adults aged 65 and older were the most likely of any group to volunteer.
Volunteers aged 18–29 averaged 120 hours, compared with 42 hours for those 65 and older.
22% of adults 65 and older volunteered, compared with 31% of those aged 18–29, but volunteers 65 and older averaged 120 hours, nearly three times the 42 hours averaged by the youngest volunteers.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo ikki qismli: keksalar kamroq ko'ngilli bo'ladi (22% va 31%), ammo ko'proq vaqt sarflaydi (120 soat va 42 soat); faqat to'g'ri javob ikkalasini ham ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Paleontologists measured fossils of an early horse species from three consecutive time periods spanning a sudden global warming event.

  Period — Average global temperature relative to today — Average body mass
  Period 1 (before event) — +3°C — 5.6 kg
  Period 2 (during event) — +8°C — 3.9 kg
  Period 3 (after event) — +4°C — 5.1 kg

In many mammal lineages, smaller bodies shed heat more easily in warm climates. The paleontologists found that the horses shrank during the warming event and grew larger again as temperatures fell. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Average body mass was highest in Period 1, before the warming event.
Average body mass rose from 5.6 kg to 3.9 kg during the warming event.
Average body mass in Period 3 was greater than in Period 1.
Average body mass fell from 5.6 kg to 3.9 kg as temperatures rose from 3°C to 8°C above today's level, then rebounded to 5.1 kg as temperatures fell to 4°C above today's level.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Isish davrida tana massasi 5.6 dan 3.9 kg ga kamaygan, harorat pasaygach 5.1 kg ga qaytgan; to'g'ri javob ikkala bosqichni ham tasvirlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Economists tracked beverage purchases in a city during the year after it introduced a tax on sugary sodas.

  Beverage — Taxed? — Change in purchases
  Sugary sodas — yes — −21%
  Diet sodas — no — +4%
  Bottled water — no — +13%
  Fruit juice — no — +1%

Before the tax took effect, the economists predicted that consumers would not simply buy fewer drinks overall but would shift toward untaxed alternatives, with bottled water gaining the most. Their prediction was borne out: ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: purchases of taxed sugary sodas fell by 21%, while purchases of all three untaxed beverages rose, with bottled water increasing the most (13%).
purchases of sugary sodas fell by 21% in the year after the tax.
purchases of diet sodas rose more than purchases of bottled water did.
purchases of fruit juice fell by 1% in the year after the tax.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Bashorat uch qismli: gazli ichimliklar kamaygan (−21%), soliqsiz barcha ichimliklar oshgan va eng ko'p suv oshgan (+13%); faqat to'g'ri javob barchasini qamraydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Animal-cognition researchers presented a group of crows with the same food puzzle over four blocks of trials.

  Trial block — Share of crows solving the puzzle — Average time to solve (seconds)
  Block 1 — 20% — 142
  Block 2 — 55% — 96
  Block 3 — 85% — 51
  Block 4 — 90% — 47

Crows are known for flexible problem-solving. The researchers argue that the birds learned the puzzle rapidly at first, with the share of successful birds leveling off in later trials. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Average time to solve the puzzle decreased in every block.
The share of crows solving the puzzle rose by 35 percentage points from Block 3 to Block 4.
The share of crows solving the puzzle rose by 35 percentage points from Block 1 to Block 2 and by 30 points from Block 2 to Block 3, but by only 5 points from Block 3 to Block 4.
In Block 4, 90% of crows solved the puzzle in an average of 47 seconds.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Dastlab tez o'sish (35 va 30 punkt), keyin sekinlashish (atigi 5 punkt) kuzatilgan; bu 'avval tez, keyin barqarorlashdi' degan fikrni tasdiqlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
A tourism analyst compared international visitor numbers and hotel prices in a historic Silk Road city.

  Month — International visitors (thousands) — Average hotel room rate (USD)
  March — 42 — 58
  May — 96 — 91
  July — 71 — 74
  September — 108 — 97
  November — 35 — 52

The city's summer heat keeps many tourists away in midsummer, so spring and autumn are its busiest seasons. The analyst claims that hotel rates in the city closely tracked visitor numbers throughout the year. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Room rates rose from March to May and then fell from May to July.
The months with the most visitors, September (108,000) and May (96,000), had the highest room rates ($97 and $91), while November, with the fewest visitors (35,000), had the lowest rate ($52).
July had more visitors than May but a lower average room rate.
March had the lowest average room rate of the months listed.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Eng ko'p mehmon bo'lgan oylarda (sentyabr, may) narxlar eng yuqori, eng kam mehmonli noyabrda esa eng past; bu narx va tashriflar birga o'zgarganini ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Hydrologists compared mountain snowpack with the timing of a river's peak spring flow over five decades.

  Decade — Average April 1 snowpack — Average date of peak spring flow
  1970s — 88 cm — June 12
  1990s — 76 cm — June 3
  2010s — 59 cm — May 21

Many downstream farms depend on the river's late-spring flow for irrigation, so its timing matters. The hydrologists argue that as snowpack in the mountains has declined, the river's peak spring flow has arrived progressively earlier. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: The average date of peak spring flow was June 3 in the 1990s.
Average April 1 snowpack increased between the 1970s and the 2010s.
As average April 1 snowpack fell from 88 cm in the 1970s to 76 cm and then 59 cm, the average peak-flow date moved from June 12 to June 3 and then to May 21.
The average date of peak spring flow moved later, from May 21 to June 12.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Qor qoplami har o'n yillikda kamaygan (88 → 76 → 59 sm), eng yuqori oqim sanasi esa har safar ertaroq kelgan (12-iyun → 3-iyun → 21-may).

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
A marketing team tested two email subject lines for an online store.

  Subject line — Emails sent — Emails opened — Purchases
  Version A (asks a question) — 10,000 — 2,600 — 130
  Version B (states a discount) — 10,000 — 2,100 — 189

Marketers often judge subject lines by how many people open the email. The team found, however, that although Version A was opened more often, Version B was more effective at producing purchases, both overall and among recipients who opened the email. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Version B produced 189 purchases versus 130 for Version A, and 9% of those who opened Version B made a purchase, compared with 5% of those who opened Version A.
Version A was opened by 2,600 recipients, compared with 2,100 for Version B.
Version B produced more purchases overall, but a smaller share of its openers made a purchase.
Both versions of the email were sent to 10,000 recipients.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: B umumiy xaridda ustun (189 va 130) va ochganlar orasida ham: 189/2100 = 9%, 130/2600 = 5%; ikkala shart ham bajariladi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Biologists compared anole lizards from two urban populations and two forest populations.

  Population — Habitat — Average hind-limb length — Sprint speed on smooth surfaces
  1 — urban — 24.8 mm — 1.9 m/s
  2 — urban — 25.3 mm — 2.0 m/s
  3 — forest — 22.1 mm — 1.4 m/s
  4 — forest — 21.7 mm — 1.3 m/s

City lizards frequently run across walls and pavement rather than tree bark. The biologists hypothesize that urban lizards have evolved longer hind limbs, which allow them to sprint faster on such smooth surfaces. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Both urban populations had longer average hind limbs (24.8 and 25.3 mm) and faster sprint speeds on smooth surfaces (1.9 and 2.0 m/s) than both forest populations did.
Population 2 had the longest average hind limbs of any population.
The forest populations sprinted faster on smooth surfaces than the urban populations did.
Population 3 had longer average hind limbs than Population 1 did.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Ikkala shahar populyatsiyasining oyoqlari ham uzunroq, ham silliq yuzada tezroq; gipoteza ikkala xususiyatni bog'laydi, to'g'ri javob ikkalasini ham ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage:
Entomologists counted moths captured each night near three types of streetlights and at dark control sites 50 meters away.

  Streetlight type — Moths near lamp — Moths at dark site
  Sodium lamp — 38 — 12
  White LED — 61 — 11
  Amber LED — 15 — 13

Many cities are replacing old sodium streetlights with energy-efficient white LEDs. The entomologists warn that this switch could worsen light pollution's effects on insects, but they suggest amber LEDs as an alternative that attracts moths barely more than darkness does. ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
choices: Sodium lamps drew 38 moths per night, compared with 12 at their dark site.
White LEDs drew fewer moths per night than sodium lamps did.
Amber LEDs drew 15 moths per night, close to the 13 captured at their dark site, whereas white LEDs drew 61 moths, compared with 11 at their dark site.
Amber LEDs drew 61 moths per night, compared with 13 at their dark site.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Qahrabo LED 15 ta kapalak jalb qilgan, qorong'i joyda esa 13 ta — deyarli farq yo'q; oq LED esa 61 taga (11 ga nisbatan) yetgan.

Inferences.passage: Composer Florence Price, the first Black woman to have a symphony performed by a major American orchestra, often incorporated melodies and rhythms from African American spirituals into works written in European classical forms. For decades after her death in 1953, much of her music went unperformed. In 2009, a large collection of her manuscripts was discovered in an abandoned house in Illinois, and orchestras soon began programming her symphonies. This sequence of events suggests that the neglect of Price's music ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: reflected her own wish that her music not be performed.
was due at least partly to limited access to her scores rather than solely to audiences' lack of interest.
ended before the discovery of her manuscripts in Illinois.
occurred because her works did not follow European classical forms.
Inferences.expl: Qo'lyozmalar topilgach orkestrlar tez orada uning simfoniyalarini ijro eta boshlagan; demak e'tiborsizlik qisman partituralarga kirish imkoni yo'qligidan bo'lgan.

Inferences.passage: The Bayeux Tapestry, which depicts the Norman conquest of England in 1066, has traditionally been attributed to Norman artisans working for the victorious William the Conqueror. The embroidery, nearly 70 meters long, was likely commissioned by William's half-brother, Bishop Odo. Art historian Gale Owen-Crocker, however, observes that its stitching techniques closely match those found in surviving Anglo-Saxon embroidery, and that several Latin inscriptions on it use spellings typical of English rather than French scribes. Owen-Crocker's observations suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the tapestry depicts an English victory over the Normans.
Anglo-Saxon embroiderers learned their techniques from Norman artisans.
the tapestry was created in France long after the conquest.
the tapestry may have been made by English workers even though it celebrates a Norman victory.
Inferences.expl: Tikish usullari anglo-sakson kashtachiligiga mos va yozuvlar ingliz kotiblariga xos imloda; demak gilamni normanlar g'alabasini ulug'lasa ham inglizlar tikkan bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: Some exoplanets orbit so close to their stars that one side always faces the star while the other remains in permanent darkness. Astronomers once assumed that such planets would have scorching day sides and frozen night sides, making them uninhabitable. However, climate models developed by physicist Aomawa Shields show that if such a planet has a thick atmosphere or deep oceans, winds and currents could carry heat from the day side to the night side. These models suggest that whether such planets could support liquid water ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: depends only on how close the planet is to its star.
may depend on characteristics of the planet beyond its orbit and rotation.
is impossible regardless of the planet's atmosphere.
has already been confirmed by direct observation of their night sides.
Inferences.expl: Modellar qalin atmosfera yoki chuqur okean issiqlikni tarqatishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi; demak suyuq suv imkoniyati orbitadan tashqari sayyora xususiyatlariga bog'liq.

Inferences.passage: Plants of the species Arabidopsis thaliana flower earlier after experiencing a prolonged period of cold, a process known as vernalization. Geneticist Wen Liu found that cold exposure gradually switches off a gene that normally blocks flowering, and that the gene remains switched off even after temperatures rise again. However, when the plants produced seeds, the gene was reactivated in the next generation. Liu's findings imply that the effect of cold exposure ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: causes the plant to stop flowering permanently.
is inherited by all future generations of the plant.
persists within an individual plant but is not passed on to its offspring.
disappears as soon as warm temperatures return in spring.
Inferences.expl: Gen isish qaytgandan keyin ham o'chiq qoladi, lekin keyingi avlodda qayta faollashadi; demak ta'sir bitta o'simlikda saqlanadi, avlodga o'tmaydi.

Inferences.passage: Elephants communicate using low-frequency rumbles that can travel several kilometers through the air and even through the ground. Biologist Caitlin O'Connell observed that elephants sometimes froze in place, leaned forward, and pressed a foot firmly to the ground when distant herds were rumbling, even when the sounds were too faint to hear through the air. Researchers later found that elephant feet contain sensitive receptors similar to those in human fingertips. These observations suggest that elephants ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: are unable to hear low-frequency sounds through the air.
use their feet to produce the rumbles that other elephants hear.
may detect distant rumbles through vibrations in the ground.
communicate only with elephants in their own herd.
Inferences.expl: Fillar oyog'ini yerga bosib turgan va oyoqlarida sezgir retseptorlar bor; demak ular uzoqdagi tovushlarni yer tebranishi orqali sezishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: Coral reefs grow as tiny animals called polyps build skeletons of calcium carbonate, a mineral they extract from seawater. As oceans absorb more carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, seawater becomes more acidic, and experiments show that polyps in more acidic water build their skeletons more slowly. Marine biologist Ana Fonseca notes that reefs are also constantly worn away by waves and by animals that bore into the coral. If ocean acidity continues to rise, Fonseca suggests, some reefs ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: will no longer be affected by waves or by boring animals.
will move to freshwater lakes where acidity is lower.
will grow faster because polyps will use carbon dioxide to build skeletons.
may begin to erode faster than the polyps can rebuild them.
Inferences.expl: Kislotalilik oshsa, poliplar skeletni sekinroq quradi, riflar esa doimo yemirilib turadi; demak yemirilish qurilishdan tezlashishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: Octopuses have a remarkable ability to change the color and texture of their skin, yet most species are thought to be colorblind, since their eyes contain only one type of light-sensitive pigment. Researchers recently discovered that octopus skin contains opsins, the same light-detecting proteins found in eyes. In laboratory tests, patches of skin removed from the animal still changed color when exposed to light, even though they were no longer connected to the eyes or brain. These findings raise the possibility that octopus skin ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: is controlled entirely by the brain when it changes color.
contains no pigments and therefore cannot change color on its own.
may be able to sense light directly, which could help explain how octopuses match their surroundings.
allows octopuses to see colors more clearly than any other animal can.
Inferences.expl: Teri ko'z va miyadan ajratilgandan keyin ham yorug'likka javob bergan; bu teri yorug'likni bevosita sezishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi.

Inferences.passage: Before the invention of refrigeration, ice was harvested from frozen lakes in New England each winter, packed in sawdust, and shipped as far away as India. Although a large portion of each shipment melted during the months-long voyage, merchants such as Frederic Tudor still made substantial profits. In hot ports where no natural ice existed, customers were willing to pay high prices for even small amounts of it. This suggests that Tudor's business succeeded because ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: most customers in India preferred ice to refrigerators.
the high value of ice in hot places outweighed the loss from melting during shipping.
ice was cheaper in India than it was in New England.
sawdust completely prevented ice from melting on long ocean voyages.
Inferences.expl: Muzning katta qismi erib ketgan bo'lsa-da, issiq portlarda unga yuqori narx to'langan; demak yuqori qiymat erish zararidan ustun kelgan.

Inferences.passage: Stone tools found at a site in Kenya called Lomekwi are about 3.3 million years old, roughly 700,000 years older than the earliest known fossils assigned to the genus Homo, the group that includes modern humans. Anthropologist Sonia Harmand notes that no Homo fossils have been found at Lomekwi, but fossils of another hominin species, Kenyanthropus platyops, have been found in nearby sediments of a similar age. Unless older Homo fossils are eventually discovered, the Lomekwi tools indicate that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: toolmaking was not limited to members of the genus Homo.
Kenyanthropus platyops was a direct ancestor of modern humans.
the earliest Homo fossils have been incorrectly dated.
stone tools were first made in regions outside of Africa.
Inferences.expl: Qurollar ma'lum Homo qoldiqlaridan 700 ming yil qadimiyroq; kattaroq Homo topilmasa, qurol yasash faqat Homo turkumiga xos bo'lmagan degan xulosa kelib chiqadi.

Inferences.passage: Novelist Chinua Achebe wrote his most famous works in English rather than in Igbo, his first language. Some critics argued that writing in a colonial language distanced Achebe from the Nigerian culture he portrayed. Achebe, however, filled his English prose with Igbo proverbs, rhythms, and storytelling patterns, and he explained that he wanted an English that was still in full communion with its ancestral home but altered to suit its new African surroundings. This suggests that Achebe viewed English as a language that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: ought to be used in literature without any outside influences.
could be reshaped to express an African cultural perspective.
was incapable of conveying the experiences of Nigerian people.
should replace Igbo as the primary language spoken in Nigeria.
Inferences.expl: Achebe ingliz tilini igbo maqollari va ritmlari bilan to'ldirgan va uni Afrika muhitiga moslashtirishni istagan; demak u ingliz tilini Afrika nuqtai nazarini ifodalash uchun o'zgartirish mumkin deb bilgan.

Inferences.passage: Some of the world's oldest known cave paintings, found in Indonesia and Spain, have been dated to more than 40,000 years ago. Because the Spanish examples predate the arrival of modern humans in Europe by some estimates, researchers have debated whether Neanderthals made them. Archaeologist Dirk Hoffmann dated mineral crusts that formed over several Spanish paintings and found that they were at least 64,000 years old, about 20,000 years before modern humans are known to have reached the region. If Hoffmann's dates are accurate, they imply that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: cave painting originated in Indonesia rather than in Europe.
the Indonesian paintings were copies of the Spanish paintings.
Neanderthals were capable of producing symbolic art.
modern humans reached Spain 20,000 years earlier than previously thought.
Inferences.expl: Rasmlar zamonaviy odamlar kelishidan 20 ming yil oldin chizilgan bo'lsa, ularni neandertallar yaratgan; demak neandertallar ramziy san'atga qodir bo'lgan.

Inferences.passage: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of kilometers to overwintering sites in central Mexico, yet no individual butterfly completes the round trip; the journey spans several generations. Researchers have shown that monarchs use the sun's position to navigate, which requires them to account for the sun's movement across the sky during the day. When biologist Steven Reppert kept monarchs under artificial light cycles that were shifted six hours from the natural day, the butterflies flew in consistently wrong directions when released. This result suggests that monarch navigation ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: is unaffected by the timing of light the butterflies experience.
depends primarily on landmarks such as mountains and rivers.
relies on an internal sense of time that helps the butterflies interpret the sun's position.
is learned from older butterflies that previously completed the journey.
Inferences.expl: Yorug'lik sikli olti soatga surilganda kapalaklar noto'g'ri yo'nalishda uchgan; demak navigatsiya quyosh holatini talqin qilish uchun ichki vaqt hissiga tayanadi.

Inferences.passage: In a well-known experiment, children who were offered one marshmallow immediately or two if they waited fifteen minutes showed varying abilities to delay gratification, and those who waited longer tended to have better academic outcomes years later. Psychologist Celeste Kidd later ran a version in which, before the test, an adult either kept or broke a promise to bring the children better art supplies. Children who had experienced the broken promise waited, on average, only about three minutes, compared with twelve minutes for the others. Kidd's results suggest that a child's decision to wait ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: may depend substantially on whether the child expects the promised reward to actually arrive.
has no relationship to the child's previous experiences with adults.
is determined entirely by a fixed personality trait present from birth.
is longer when children have recently been disappointed by adults.
Inferences.expl: Va'dasi buzilgan bolalar ancha qisqa kutgan; demak kutish qarori mukofot haqiqatan kelishiga ishonishga katta darajada bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: Japanese woodblock prints of the Edo period were often produced in large editions, sometimes thousands of copies, and sold cheaply to ordinary city dwellers. Each color required its own carved block, and the blocks wore down slightly with every impression. Art historian Keiko Morimoto explains that collectors today pay the highest prices for early impressions, in which lines are sharpest and colors align precisely. Given this information, a print from late in a large edition would likely ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: show less crisp lines than a print made early in the same edition.
have been sold for a higher price than early prints during the Edo period.
contain more colors than prints made at the beginning of the edition.
have been carved from an entirely new set of blocks for each copy.
Inferences.expl: Bloklar har bir nusxadan keyin biroz yeyiladi, shuning uchun nashrning oxirgi nusxalarida chiziqlar erta nusxalardagiga qaraganda kamroq aniq bo'ladi.

Inferences.passage: Sociologist Kiran Mehta examined why some neighborhoods recover faster than others after natural disasters. Neighborhoods with higher average incomes did tend to rebuild more quickly, but Mehta found an important exception: several low-income neighborhoods in her sample rebuilt as fast as wealthy ones. These neighborhoods had dense networks of local organizations, such as religious congregations and mutual aid groups, that helped residents share tools, labor, and information about aid programs. Mehta concluded that, although income matters, ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: wealth has no connection to how quickly neighborhoods recover from disasters.
strong community ties may help neighborhoods overcome some of the disadvantages of lower income.
low-income neighborhoods generally recover faster than wealthy ones.
local organizations slow recovery by duplicating government aid.
Inferences.expl: Kam daromadli, lekin mahalliy tashkilotlari zich bo'lgan mahallalar boylar kabi tez tiklangan; demak kuchli jamoaviy aloqalar daromad kamchiligini qisman yengishga yordam beradi.

Inferences.passage: Volcanologists monitor sulfur dioxide gas released from volcanoes because rising emissions can signal that magma is moving toward the surface. At one volcano, however, researchers led by Hanna Lindqvist observed that sulfur dioxide emissions fell sharply in the weeks before a major eruption. Measurements also showed the ground above the volcano swelling during that period. Lindqvist proposed that the gas had become trapped beneath a hardened plug of rock. If her explanation is correct, it would suggest that a drop in sulfur dioxide emissions ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: does not necessarily indicate that a volcano is becoming less likely to erupt.
is the most reliable sign that an eruption has already ended.
always means that magma has begun to move away from the surface.
occurs only at volcanoes that never experience major eruptions.
Inferences.expl: Gaz qotgan tosh tiqini ostida qolib ketgan bo'lsa, gaz chiqishining kamayishi otilish ehtimoli pasayganini anglatmaydi; aksincha bosim ortishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: Psychologist Amara Nwosu asked participants to memorize a list of words either by reading them silently or by reading them aloud. Participants who read aloud later recalled significantly more words. In a follow-up study, a third group listened to a recording of someone else reading the words aloud; this group recalled more words than silent readers but fewer than those who read aloud themselves. Nwosu concluded that the memory advantage of reading aloud ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: results partly from hearing the words and partly from producing them oneself.
is smaller than the advantage of reading silently.
disappears when participants hear someone else read the words.
comes entirely from hearing the words rather than from speaking them.
Inferences.expl: Tinglovchilar jim o'quvchilardan yaxshiroq, ammo o'zi ovoz chiqarib o'qiganlardan yomonroq eslagan; demak afzallik ham eshitishdan, ham o'zi talaffuz qilishdan kelib chiqadi.

Inferences.passage: In the 1850s, many American newspapers began printing weather reports supplied by telegraph operators in distant towns. Before the telegraph, a storm could move faster than any written warning about it, because letters traveled only as fast as horses or trains. Historian Marcus Adeyemi notes that once telegraph lines connected towns across hundreds of miles, operators in western cities could report approaching storms to eastern cities before the storms arrived. Adeyemi suggests that, as a result, the telegraph ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: allowed scientists to prevent storms from reaching eastern cities.
caused newspapers to stop printing any news that was not related to the weather.
was used mainly by farmers rather than by newspaper publishers.
made it possible for people to receive advance warning of some storms for the first time.
Inferences.expl: Matnga ko'ra, telegrafdan oldin ogohlantirish bo'rondan tezroq yetib bora olmagan; telegraf esa bo'ron kelishidan oldin xabar berishga imkon bergan.

Inferences.passage: Behavioral ecologists have observed that female túngara frogs prefer males whose calls include complex chuck sounds over males with simpler calls. Calling with chucks, however, also attracts frog-eating bats, which locate prey by sound. Researcher Ximena Bernal found that males in ponds with many bats produced chucks far less often than males in ponds with few bats, and that males quickly reduced chuck calls when bat sounds were played through speakers. Bernal's findings suggest that male túngara frogs ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: are unable to detect the presence of bats nearby.
adjust their calls to balance attracting mates against the risk of being eaten.
attract more females in ponds where bats are common.
never produce chuck sounds when females are present.
Inferences.expl: Erkaklar ko'rshapalaklar ko'p bo'lganda murakkab tovushlarni kamaytiradi; demak ular juft jalb qilish va yeyilish xavfi o'rtasida muvozanat saqlaydi.

Inferences.passage: Linguist Priya Raman studied how children in bilingual households learn words for colors. She found that children exposed to two languages often learned color words slightly later than children exposed to one language. However, by age six, the bilingual children knew color words in both languages, giving them a larger total vocabulary for colors than monolingual children of the same age. Raman's findings suggest that an early delay in learning color words ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: causes bilingual children to confuse colors for the rest of their lives.
shows that learning two languages harms a child's ability to see colors.
occurs only in children who learn languages with few color words.
does not prevent bilingual children from eventually knowing more color terms overall.
Inferences.expl: Ikki tilli bolalar dastlab kechikkan bo'lsa-da, olti yoshga kelib ikkala tilda rang so'zlarini bilgan; demak kechikish ularning oxir-oqibat ko'proq so'z bilishiga to'sqinlik qilmaydi.

Inferences.passage: In the nineteenth century, the photographer Julia Margaret Cameron was criticized for producing portraits that were slightly out of focus, a quality that many of her contemporaries considered a technical failure. Most portrait photographers of the era aimed for the crisp, precise detail that the new medium made possible. Cameron, however, deliberately adjusted her lenses to soften the images and wrote that she sought to capture the inner character of her subjects rather than every detail of their faces. This suggests that Cameron ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: valued emotional expression in her portraits more than sharp detail.
lacked the technical skill needed to produce sharply focused images.
believed photography should record faces as precisely as possible.
agreed with critics that her photographs were failures.
Inferences.expl: Kemeron linzalarni ataylab sozlagan va yuz tafsilotlaridan ko'ra ichki xarakterni ifodalashni istagan; demak u hissiy ifodani aniq tafsilotdan ustun qo'ygan.

Inferences.passage: Many songbirds learn their songs by listening to adult males during a sensitive period early in life. Biologist Yusuf Karaman raised young zebra finches in two groups: one heard recordings of adult song, while the other heard recordings and also interacted with a live adult male tutor. Both groups heard the same number of song repetitions. At maturity, birds with live tutors produced songs that matched the adult model far more closely than did birds exposed only to recordings. Karaman's results suggest that for young zebra finches, ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: recordings of adult song interfere with the ability to learn from live birds.
the number of times a song is heard is the only factor that affects learning.
social interaction with a tutor contributes to song learning beyond simply hearing the song.
song learning can occur at any point in life rather than during a sensitive period.
Inferences.expl: Ikkala guruh bir xil miqdorda qo'shiq eshitgan, ammo jonli ustozli qushlar yaxshiroq o'rgangan; demak ijtimoiy muloqot eshitishdan tashqari qo'shimcha hissa qo'shadi.

Inferences.passage: Researchers tracked how long it took commuters in one city to travel to work before and after a new rapid bus lane opened on the city's busiest avenue. For riders on buses using the avenue, average commute times dropped by twelve minutes. Drivers of private cars on the same avenue saw almost no change in their travel times, while drivers on parallel streets experienced slightly longer trips. The researchers suspected that some drivers ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: had shifted to parallel streets after one car lane on the avenue became a bus lane.
preferred the avenue because it now offered faster car travel.
had stopped driving to work altogether and begun walking.
were unaware that the bus lane had been built on the avenue.
Inferences.expl: Parallel ko'chalarda safar biroz uzaygan; bu ba'zi haydovchilar avenyudan parallel ko'chalarga o'tganini ko'rsatadi.

Inferences.passage: The ancient city of Petra, in present-day Jordan, was built in a dry region that receives very little rain each year, and no permanent river flows through it. Yet archaeologists have found that Petra supported a population of perhaps 20,000 people at its height. Throughout the city, the Nabataeans who lived there carved channels into rock walls, built dams across narrow valleys, and dug large underground cisterns. These discoveries suggest that the Nabataeans ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: relied mainly on rivers that flowed through the center of the city.
abandoned Petra because they were unable to find sources of water.
developed methods for capturing and storing the limited rainfall their region received.
lived in Petra only during the rare years when rain was plentiful.
Inferences.expl: Kanallar, to'g'onlar va yer osti sardobalari nabatiylar kam yog'ingarchilikni yig'ish va saqlash usullarini ishlab chiqqanini ko'rsatadi.

Inferences.passage: Many desert plants open the tiny pores on their leaves, called stomata, only at night. Plants need open stomata to take in carbon dioxide, but open pores also let water vapor escape. Because desert nights are much cooler and more humid than desert days, a plant loses far less water through open stomata after sunset. Botanists therefore view nighttime pore opening as a strategy that allows desert plants to ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: avoid taking in carbon dioxide during the hottest hours of the year.
absorb water vapor from the air through their stomata during the day.
grow faster than plants that live in humid tropical forests.
obtain carbon dioxide while limiting water loss in a dry environment.
Inferences.expl: Tunda teshikchalarni ochish o'simlikka karbonat angidridni olish bilan birga suv yo'qotishni kamaytirish imkonini beradi.

Inferences.passage: A small publishing company released the same novel in two formats: a hardcover edition priced at $28 and an e-book priced at $9. During the first month, the e-book sold four times as many copies as the hardcover. However, in bookstores that hosted in-person readings by the author, hardcover sales were much higher than in stores that did not host readings, and in those stores the hardcover outsold the e-book. The company's marketing director concluded that author readings ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: reduce overall interest in the novel among readers who prefer e-books.
should be replaced by lowering the price of the hardcover edition.
are the only reason that anyone bought the e-book edition of the novel.
may encourage readers to purchase the more expensive physical edition of a book.
Inferences.expl: Kitobxonlik tadbirlari o'tkazilgan do'konlarda qattiq muqovali nashr ko'proq sotilgan; bu tadbirlar qimmatroq jismoniy nashrni sotib olishga undashi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi.

Inferences.passage: In 1927, American aviator Charles Lindbergh completed the first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic Ocean. To carry enough fuel for the 33-hour journey, he removed nearly every nonessential item from his plane, including a radio and a parachute. He even chose a plane design in which an extra fuel tank blocked his forward view, so he had to look out the side windows to see ahead. These choices indicate that Lindbergh ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: considered carrying extra fuel more important than several comforts and safety features.
believed a radio would have been useful only on flights over land.
was not concerned about whether he would complete the flight.
wanted to prove that pilots did not need to see where they were flying.
Inferences.expl: Lindberg qo'shimcha yoqilg'i uchun radio, parashyut va hatto oldingi ko'rinishdan voz kechgan; demak u yoqilg'ini qulaylik va xavfsizlik vositalaridan muhimroq deb bilgan.

Inferences.passage: In medieval Europe, most books were copied by hand in monasteries, and a single manuscript could take a scribe many months to complete. Historian Elena Vasquez has examined surviving account books from several fifteenth-century monasteries and found that, in the decades after the printing press spread, payments to scribes dropped sharply while purchases of printed books rose. Yet the same records show that monasteries continued to pay scribes for decorated liturgical books used in religious services. Vasquez's evidence suggests that after printing spread, handwritten manuscripts ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: remained valued for certain specialized purposes even as printed books took over general copying.
were produced only for readers who could not afford printed books.
became more common than printed books in most monastery libraries.
disappeared completely from monasteries within a few years.
Inferences.expl: Kotiblarga to'lovlar umuman kamaygan, ammo bezatilgan diniy kitoblar uchun davom etgan; demak qo'lyozmalar maxsus maqsadlar uchun qadrlanishda davom etgan.

Inferences.passage: Chefs have long debated whether salting eggplant before cooking removes bitterness. Food scientist Tomás Varela had volunteers taste eggplant slices, some salted and rinsed and some untreated. When the eggplants came from older varieties, tasters consistently rated untreated slices as more bitter. But for modern varieties, which breeders developed over recent decades, tasters could not tell the salted and untreated slices apart. Varela's results suggest that modern eggplant varieties ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: are probably less bitter to begin with than older varieties are.
become more bitter than older varieties after being salted.
are preferred by most tasters over older eggplant varieties.
should never be salted before being cooked by chefs.
Inferences.expl: Zamonaviy navlarda tuzlangan va tuzlanmagan bo'laklar farqlanmagan; bu ular dastlabdanoq kamroq achchiq ekanini ko'rsatadi.

Inferences.passage: In the 1970s, several Latin American governments pursued import substitution, raising tariffs on foreign manufactured goods to encourage domestic factories. Initially, industrial output rose substantially. Economist Marisol Ferreira examined firm-level data from Brazil and found that the protected firms that grew most rapidly were those that exported part of their production, since exporting forced them to compete with international rivals on price and quality. Protected firms that sold only in the domestic market showed little improvement in productivity over the same period. Ferreira's findings suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: tariffs on foreign goods caused domestic industrial output to decline immediately.
firms that sold only domestically grew faster than exporting firms.
exposure to foreign competition, rather than tariff protection alone, may have driven productivity gains.
Brazilian firms were unable to export any goods while tariffs were in place.
Inferences.expl: Himoyalangan firmalardan faqat eksport qilganlari tez rivojlangan, faqat ichki bozorda sotganlari esa deyarli o'smagan; demak unumdorlik o'sishini tariflar emas, xalqaro raqobat ta'minlagan.

Inferences.passage: Economic historians have long noted that countries with more navigable rivers tended to industrialize earlier in the nineteenth century, and many have argued that cheap river transport directly spurred factory growth. Economist Tobias Engel points out, however, that regions with navigable rivers also tended to have older, denser cities, which had developed banking networks and skilled labor pools centuries before industrialization. When Engel compared river regions with non-river regions that had cities of similar age and size, the difference in industrialization timing largely disappeared. Engel's analysis suggests that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: banking networks developed only after factories were built along rivers.
river transport was more expensive than land transport during the nineteenth century.
the link between rivers and early industrialization may reflect the influence of pre-existing urban development.
regions without navigable rivers industrialized earlier than regions with them.
Inferences.expl: Shaharlari o'xshash bo'lgan hududlar solishtirilganda farq yo'qolgan; demak daryolar va sanoatlashuv bog'liqligi avvaldan mavjud shahar rivojlanishini aks ettirishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: Economists have documented that people often continue investing in failing projects because of the resources they have already committed, a tendency known as the sunk cost effect. Researcher Hal Arkes asked participants to imagine they had paid for two nonrefundable ski trips that turned out to be scheduled for the same weekend: a $100 trip and a $50 trip they expected to enjoy more. More than half chose the $100 trip. Arkes's results suggest that many participants ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: preferred the $50 trip but chose it less often because it was cheaper to cancel.
correctly chose the option that would give them the greatest enjoyment.
let the amount previously spent outweigh their expectation of which option they would enjoy more.
believed that the more expensive trip would be refunded if they skipped it.
Inferences.expl: Ishtirokchilar ko'proq zavq kutgan 50 dollarlik sayohat o'rniga 100 dollarlikni tanlagan; demak sarflangan pul miqdori kutilgan zavqdan ustun kelgan.

Inferences.passage: Deep-sea anglerfish live in waters where little food is available and potential mates are rare. In some species, a tiny male permanently attaches himself to a much larger female, eventually fusing with her body and sharing her bloodstream. Immunologist Jeremy Swann found that these species lack several genes that, in most vertebrates, cause the immune system to attack foreign tissue. Species in which males do not fuse with females retain those genes. Swann's findings suggest that the loss of these immune genes ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: occurred in every species of deep-sea fish regardless of mating behavior.
may have been necessary for permanent fusion between males and females to evolve.
made anglerfish better able to reject foreign tissue.
caused anglerfish males to grow larger than females.
Inferences.expl: Faqat erkak va urg'ochisi qo'shiladigan turlarda begona to'qimaga hujum qiluvchi genlar yo'q; demak bu genlarning yo'qolishi doimiy qo'shilish evolyutsiyasi uchun zarur bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: During the 1930s Dust Bowl, severe drought and poor farming practices stripped topsoil from the American Great Plains, and many farming families migrated west. Historians have often attributed the migration primarily to the dust storms themselves. However, economist Ruth Okafor found that migration rates were nearly as high in some Plains counties that experienced relatively mild erosion as in counties devastated by storms. What those mild-erosion counties shared with the hardest-hit counties was a steep drop in crop prices and a high rate of farm foreclosures. Okafor's findings suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: economic pressures may have played a larger role in the migration than is often assumed.
dust storms had no effect at all on farmers' decisions to leave the Plains.
crop prices rose in counties that experienced mild erosion.
families in severely eroded counties were less likely to migrate than others.
Inferences.expl: Eroziya yengil bo'lgan okruglarda ham migratsiya yuqori bo'lgan va ularni narx tushishi hamda musodaralar birlashtirgan; demak iqtisodiy bosim muhimroq rol o'ynagan bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: Urban planners in Medellín, Colombia, built a series of cable cars in the 2000s to connect hillside neighborhoods to the city's metro system. Previously, residents of these neighborhoods often spent more than an hour walking and taking buses to reach jobs downtown. A later study found that employment rates in neighborhoods served by cable cars rose faster than in similar hillside neighborhoods without them, even though the types of jobs available downtown did not change. The study's authors reasoned that the cable cars likely ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: caused businesses to move from downtown into the hillside neighborhoods.
created most of the new jobs that hillside residents obtained.
made jobs downtown more accessible to hillside residents by shortening their commutes.
were used primarily by tourists rather than by local residents.
Inferences.expl: Ish turlari o'zgarmagan, ammo kanat yo'li bor mahallalarda bandlik tezroq o'sgan; bu yo'lning qisqargani ishlarga yetib borishni osonlashtirganini bildiradi.

Inferences.passage: Researchers studying urban gardens in Detroit measured the levels of lead in vegetables grown in soil that had once been near busy roads or factories. Leafy greens such as lettuce contained noticeably more lead than fruiting crops such as tomatoes. Further tests showed that most of the lead on the lettuce was in soil particles clinging to the leaves rather than inside the plant tissue, and thorough washing removed most of it. The findings suggest that gardeners in such areas ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: cannot safely eat any vegetable grown in urban soil.
could reduce their exposure to lead by carefully washing leafy vegetables before eating them.
should grow only lettuce because it absorbs less lead than tomatoes.
would be exposed to more lead from tomatoes than from lettuce.
Inferences.expl: Qo'rg'oshinning ko'p qismi barglarga yopishgan tuproqda bo'lib, yuvish uni olib tashlagan; demak yaxshilab yuvish ta'sirni kamaytiradi.

Inferences.passage: The painter Tarsila do Amaral, a central figure in Brazilian modernism, studied in Paris during the 1920s alongside several leading European artists, absorbing the techniques of Cubism and other avant-garde movements. When she returned to Brazil, however, she began painting scenes of Brazilian landscapes, plants, and folk traditions using the bold colors and simplified forms she had learned abroad. Critics have described her work from this period as a blend of ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: European modernist techniques and distinctly Brazilian subjects.
styles she invented without any influence from other artists.
realistic European portraiture and abstract Brazilian music.
traditional Brazilian techniques and scenes of Parisian streets.
Inferences.expl: Tarsila Parijda o'rgangan yorqin ranglar va soddalashtirilgan shakllarni Braziliya manzaralari va an'analariga qo'llagan.

Inferences.passage: The Andean city of Cusco sits at an altitude of about 3,400 meters, where each breath contains roughly one-third less oxygen than a breath taken at sea level. Visitors who fly directly to Cusco from coastal cities often experience headaches and fatigue during their first days. Travelers who instead spend several days in towns at intermediate altitudes before reaching Cusco report these symptoms far less often. This pattern suggests that the human body ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: requires more oxygen in coastal cities than it does in mountain towns.
responds to high altitude in exactly the same way for every traveler.
cannot function normally at any altitude higher than sea level.
can gradually adjust to lower oxygen levels if given time to do so.
Inferences.expl: Oraliq balandlikda bir necha kun o'tkazganlarda alomatlar kamroq uchraydi; demak organizm vaqt berilsa kislorod kamligiga asta-sekin moslashadi.

Inferences.passage: Critics have frequently described the Victorian novelist George Eliot's fiction as pessimistic, pointing to the many characters whose ambitions end in disappointment. Literary scholar Nadia Haddad offers a different reading. She observes that Eliot's narrators consistently emphasize how the small, unrecorded actions of these characters improve the lives of those around them, as in the final line of Middlemarch, which credits the growing good of the world partly to people who lived faithfully a hidden life. Haddad suggests that, rather than being purely pessimistic, Eliot's novels ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: celebrate only characters who fulfill their greatest ambitions.
locate a kind of significance in ordinary lives that do not achieve grand ambitions.
were intended by Eliot to be read as comedies.
reject the idea that individual actions can affect other people.
Inferences.expl: Haddadga ko'ra, Eliot hikoyachilari muvaffaqiyatsiz qahramonlarning kichik harakatlari boshqalar hayotini yaxshilashini ta'kidlaydi; demak romanlar oddiy hayotda ahamiyat topadi.

Inferences.passage: Many historians once believed that the Silk Road was primarily a route for luxury goods such as silk and spices carried by long-distance merchants traveling from China to the Mediterranean. Archaeologist Farida Nurmatova, however, analyzed goods found at settlements along the route in Central Asia and discovered that most items were everyday objects, such as pottery, tools, and grain, produced within a few hundred kilometers of where they were found. Nurmatova's findings suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: long-distance merchants carried mostly pottery and grain from China.
silk and spices were never transported along the Silk Road.
Central Asian settlements did not participate in trade of any kind.
much of the trade along the Silk Road may have been regional rather than long-distance.
Inferences.expl: Topilgan buyumlarning ko'pchiligi yaqin atrofda ishlab chiqarilgan kundalik narsalar bo'lgan; demak savdoning katta qismi mintaqaviy bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: Astronomers can estimate the age of a star cluster by examining which of its stars have begun to swell into red giants. Massive stars burn through their fuel quickly and become red giants early, while smaller stars remain stable for billions of years. In a cluster observed by astronomer Dmitri Volkov, even stars only slightly more massive than the Sun had already become red giants. Volkov therefore concluded that the cluster ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: will soon produce many new massive stars.
consists entirely of stars that are less massive than the Sun.
formed very recently and contains no stable stars.
is relatively old, since even moderately sized stars have used up much of their fuel.
Inferences.expl: Katta yulduzlar erta qizil gigantga aylanadi; hatto Quyoshdan sal kattaroq yulduzlar ham qizil gigant bo'lgani to'dani nisbatan qadimiy ekanini ko'rsatadi.

Inferences.passage: Tardigrades, microscopic animals sometimes called water bears, can survive being completely dried out for years. When water returns, they revive within hours. Researchers studying one tardigrade species found that, as the animals dried, they produced large amounts of a protein that forms a glass-like gel inside their cells. When scientists inserted the gene for this protein into yeast, the yeast survived drying far better than ordinary yeast did. These results suggest that the protein ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: is found in every organism that can survive without water.
allows tardigrades to live without water permanently.
helps protect cells from damage caused by drying out.
is harmful to organisms other than tardigrades.
Inferences.expl: Oqsil geni kiritilgan achitqi quritishga ancha yaxshi chidagan; demak bu oqsil hujayralarni qurishdan himoya qiladi.

Inferences.passage: Sea otters eat large numbers of sea urchins, which in turn feed on kelp, a type of large seaweed that forms underwater forests. Along parts of the Pacific coast where otters were hunted nearly to extinction in the 1800s, urchin populations grew rapidly and kelp forests shrank dramatically. In the twentieth century, otters were protected by law and gradually returned to some of these areas. Ecologists studying those coastlines would therefore most likely expect that, where otters have returned, ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: urchins have adapted by feeding on otters instead of kelp.
kelp forests have disappeared entirely because otters also eat kelp.
kelp forests have begun to recover as urchin numbers decline.
otters have been forced to leave because urchins are no longer present.
Inferences.expl: Qunduzlar dengiz tipratikanlarini yeydi, tipratikanlar esa kelpni yeydi; qunduzlar qaytgach tipratikanlar kamayib, kelp o'rmonlari tiklanishi kutiladi.

Inferences.passage: Coffee plants grown in full sun typically produce more beans per plant than those grown beneath a canopy of taller trees. For this reason, many farmers in Central America cleared shade trees during the late twentieth century. Agronomist Luis Carvajal compared sun-grown and shade-grown farms over fifteen years and found that shade-grown farms required far less fertilizer and pesticide, and their yields varied less from year to year. Carvajal's findings suggest that, over the long term, shade-grown farms ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: are less profitable than sun-grown farms in every year.
produce more beans per plant than sun-grown farms do.
cannot be maintained without heavy use of fertilizer.
may offer advantages that partly offset their lower yields per plant.
Inferences.expl: Soyada o'stirilgan fermalar kamroq o'g'it va pestitsid talab qilgan va hosili barqarorroq bo'lgan; bu past hosildorlikni qisman qoplaydigan afzalliklardir.

Inferences.passage: Historians have traditionally dated the decline of the Maya city of Copán to around 800 CE, when monument building stopped and the royal dynasty collapsed. Archaeologist David Webster, however, analyzed obsidian artifacts from rural households surrounding the city and found evidence that many of these homes remained occupied for another two centuries. Pollen records from the region also indicate that farming continued, though on a smaller scale, well after 800 CE. Webster's evidence suggests that the collapse of Copán's royal dynasty ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: was caused by rural farmers who rebelled against the city's rulers.
occurred much later than 800 CE, when monument building stopped.
led to a rapid increase in agricultural production around the city.
did not coincide with an immediate abandonment of the surrounding region.
Inferences.expl: Qishloq uylari yana ikki asr band bo'lgan va dehqonchilik davom etgan; demak sulolaning qulashi hududning darhol tashlab ketilishiga to'g'ri kelmagan.

Inferences.passage: The Voynich manuscript, a fifteenth-century book written in an unknown script, has puzzled scholars for over a century. Some have argued that it is a meaningless hoax. Linguist Marcelo Montemurro analyzed the frequency and distribution of words in the manuscript and found that certain words cluster in specific sections, such as those containing botanical illustrations, in much the same way that topic-related words cluster in texts written in known languages. Randomly generated text, by contrast, does not show such patterns. Montemurro's analysis suggests that the manuscript ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: has now been fully translated into a known language.
was written by a botanist who invented the script to record plants.
is more likely to contain meaningful language than randomly produced symbols.
is a hoax created in the twentieth century rather than the fifteenth.
Inferences.expl: So'zlar ma'lum tillardagi kabi mavzuga qarab to'planadi, tasodifiy matnda esa bunday bo'lmaydi; demak qo'lyozmada mazmunli til bo'lish ehtimoli yuqoriroq.

Inferences.passage: When a museum in Oslo began offering free admission on Thursday evenings, attendance on those evenings tripled. Surveys showed that most Thursday visitors were between 18 and 30 years old, an age group that made up only a small share of daytime visitors who paid full price. Museum staff also noted that many Thursday visitors returned later on regular paid days. Staff concluded that the free evenings may have ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
